record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

 DIRECTOR, POWER PLANT OPERATIONS 

 The Director, Memphis Power Plant Operations provides strategic and operational leadership for the gas turbine power generation facility supporting SpaceXSI's Colossus data center campus in Memphis, Tennessee. This role oversees all plant operations, maintenance, commissioning, and continued construction/expansion of the dedicated power plant, with full ownership of delivering reliable, high-availability electrical power to the Colossus AI training clusters. The position is responsible for driving operational excellence, ensuring 24/7 power reliability and quality, safety, environmental compliance, and leading cross-functional teams to achieve aggressive scale-up, availability, cost, and schedule objectives in a high-growth, fast-paced environment.

 RESPONSIBILITIES: 

 
 Provide strategic and operational leadership for the Memphis gas turbine power plant, including 24/7 operations, maintenance, commissioning, and ongoing construction and capacity expansion

 Own end-to-end delivery of electrical power to the Colossus data center sites, ensuring industry-leading reliability, availability, power quality, and redundancy

 Lead multidisciplinary teams of operators, maintenance technicians, engineers, contractors, and support staff in a 24/7 operational and construction environment

 Oversee plant performance, commissioning, testing, and seamless integration with data center electrical infrastructure and load

 Develop and execute comprehensive operations and maintenance strategies, including preventative/predictive maintenance, outage planning, hot gas path management, and OEM coordination for gas turbines, generators, balance of plant, and high-voltage electrical systems

 Manage concurrent construction, equipment installation, civil works, and phased capacity expansions while maintaining safe, reliable operation of the existing plant

 Ensure full compliance with environmental, safety, and regulatory requirements, including air permits, emissions controls, TDEC, EPA, OSHA, and local authorities

 Partner closely with SpaceXSI data center operations, engineering, fuel suppliers, OEMs, utilities, and regulatory agencies

 Formulate and execute operating budgets, fuel management, O&M, capital projects, and annual operating plans

 Drive continuous improvement in plant availability, heat rate, emissions, cost, safety metrics, and operational processes

 Establish and promote a culture of uncompromising safety, accountability, operational excellence, rapid execution, and collaboration

 Serve as the site leader and primary representative to the Memphis community, regulators, and stakeholders

 Recruit, develop, coach, and retain high-performing talent; manage staffing, resource allocation, and contractor oversight for both operations and construction

 
 BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: 

 
 Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, electrical, or other engineering discipline

 8+ years of experience in power generation operations, plant management, or industrial or aerospace operations

 5+ years of leadership experience managing teams of operators, technicians, and engineers

 Experience operating or managing gas turbine power plants (simple cycle or combined cycle)

 
 PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: 

 
 Experience managing large-scale gas turbine facilities (100 MW+), preferably with high-availability critical power applications (data centers, industrial, or similar)

 Proven track record of achieving and sustaining high plant availability, reliability, and low forced outage rates

 Hands-on experience with plant construction, commissioning, start-up, and concurrent operations/expansion of gas turbine facilities

 Deep knowledge of gas turbine technology (aeroderivative and/or heavy-duty frames), performance optimization, emissions controls (SCR, etc.), and balance of plant systems

 Experience with high-voltage electrical systems, generators, switchgear, protection, and data center or industrial interconnection

 Strong understanding of environmental permitting, air quality compliance, and regulatory reporting for combustion turbines

 Experience in fast-paced, high-growth environments requiring simultaneous operations and major construction

 Demonstrated ability to manage budgets, fuel costs, contractors, and complex stakeholder relationships

 Excellent oral and written communication, leadership, and interpersonal skills

 Unfazed by major, abrupt changes in strategic direction or aggressive timelines

 Ability to work in a demanding, autonomously driven, start-up atmosphere

 
 ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: 

 
 Ability to support and supervise plant operations and construction outside of normal business hours, including nights, weekends, and on-call response

 Must be based at the Memphis, TN site

 Willingness to work extended hours as needed to support plant reliability and construction milestones

 General physical fitness required; ability to walk the plant site, access equipment, and work in industrial/outdoor environments (heat, noise, etc.)

 SpaceXSI is an equal opportunity employer. For details on data processing, view our Recruitment Privacy Notice .

At GE Appliances, a Haier company, we come together to make “good things, for life.”  As the fastest-growing appliance company in the U.S., we’re powered by creators, thinkers and makers who believe that anything is possible and that there’s always a better way.  We believe in the power of our people and in giving them the freedom to explore, discover and build good things, together.  

 The GE Appliances philosophy, backed by three simple commitments defines the way we work, invent, create, do business, and serve our communities:  we come together ,  we always look for a better way , and  we create possibilities . 

 Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of hire and must be able to maintain such authorization without current or future employer or school sponsorship. GE Appliances will not sponsor employment-based visas for this position now or in the future.

 Interested in joining us on our journey? 

The Manufacturing Quality Director provides strategic leadership and oversight of manufacturing quality performance, ensuring operational excellence, product reliability, customer satisfaction, and continuous improvement. This position is responsible for developing and executing quality strategies, driving improvements in internal and external quality metrics, and reducing the overall cost of quality.
As a key member of the plant leadership team, the Manufacturing Quality Director partners with Operations, Manufacturing Engineering, Advanced Manufacturing Engineering, Product Management, Supplier Quality, Technology, Distribution, and Service to establish quality objectives, resolve complex quality issues, and ensure alignment with business priorities.
The Director is accountable for manufacturing quality performance, execution of the quality operating plan, continuous improvement initiatives, and leadership and development of the Quality organization.
This role supports plant operations in LaFayette, GA. 
 Position 
Manufacturing Quality Director 
 Location 
USA, LaFayette, GA 
 
 How You'll Create Possibilities 
 Quality Strategy and Operational Leadership 
 Develop and execute manufacturing quality strategies aligned with plant and business objectives.
 Provide leadership and direction for quality performance across manufacturing operations.
  
 Establish measurable quality objectives, performance targets, and improvement plans to support operational excellence.
 Partner with plant leadership and cross-functional teams to integrate quality requirements into manufacturing processes and business decisions.
 Drive accountability for quality performance through effective communication, performance reviews, and corrective action plans.
 Promote a culture of quality ownership, continuous improvement, and proactive problem-solving throughout the organization.
  
 Quality Performance and Continuous Improvement 
  
 Own and drive improvement of key internal and external quality metrics, including First Pass Yield (FPY), Cost of Quality (COQ), Service Call Rate (SCR), scrap, Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE), and product damage.
 Analyze quality performance data to identify trends, emerging risks, and opportunities for improvement.
 Lead the development and execution of corrective and preventive action (CAPA) plans to address quality concerns and prevent recurrence.
 Ensure timely containment, root cause analysis, and permanent corrective actions for End-of-Line Audit (EOLA) findings and other manufacturing quality issues.
 Drive year-over-year improvements in quality performance, process capability, and manufacturing efficiency.
 Champion Lean principles, structured problem-solving, error-proofing (poka-yoke), and proactive quality tools to reduce defects and improve process reliability.
  
 Cost of Quality and Financial Accountability 
 Own the development and execution of the manufacturing Cost of Quality operating plan.
 Identify and prioritize opportunities to reduce scrap, rework, warranty exposure, product damage, and other quality-related costs.
 Establish improvement initiatives targeting the highest contributors to quality losses.
 Partner with Operations, Finance, Engineering, and other stakeholders to evaluate financial impacts and deliver sustainable cost reductions.
 Monitor performance against quality cost targets and implement corrective actions to address unfavorable trends.
 Drive resolution of quality-related concessions attributable to manufacturing operations and implement strategies to prevent recurrence.
  
 Quality Management Systems and Process Control 
 Ensure manufacturing operations comply with established Quality Management System (QMS) requirements, applicable ISO standards, and internal quality procedures.
 Provide oversight of the Manufacturing Change Process (MCP), ensuring changes are appropriately evaluated, documented, approved, communicated, and implemented.
 Partner with the Change Implementation Board (CIB) and cross-functional stakeholders to maintain effective change control and documentation compliance.
 Identify critical manufacturing processes requiring control plans and ensure appropriate controls are established, documented, and maintained.
 Ensure manufacturing quality standards, procedures, and control plans remain current and are consistently followed.
 Support continuous improvement of quality systems, process controls, and manufacturing standards to minimize operational risk.
  
 Cross-Functional Quality and Customer Support 
  
 Collaborate with Supplier Quality, Manufacturing Engineering, Product Engineering, Advanced Manufacturing Engineering, Field Quality, Distribution, and Service to resolve quality issues impacting manufacturing operations and customers.
 Partner with Supplier Quality to address supplier-related defects, assess proposed supplier changes, and ensure appropriate change control and production readiness.
 Work with Field Quality and Service organizations to identify emerging product concerns, evaluate field performance, and implement effective manufacturing countermeasures.
 Ensure appropriate quality controls are established for product rework, reprogramming, and corrective actions performed at supplier facilities, distribution centers, or other locations.
 Support resolution of Technical Assistance Group (TAG) concerns and other field service issues attributable to manufacturing processes.
 Collaborate with Engineering to recommend improvements to product testing requirements and manufacturing controls based on field performance and customer usage.
 Leverage technical expertise across the organization to accelerate problem resolution and achieve quality objectives.
  
 People Leadership and Organizational Development 
 Lead, develop, and manage the Manufacturing Quality organization, including Quality Leaders, Quality Engineers, technical specialists, and other supporting personnel.
 Establish clear performance expectations, responsibilities, and development objectives aligned with departmental and business priorities.
 Provide coaching, mentoring, and performance feedback to strengthen technical capabilities, leadership effectiveness, and accountability.
 Ensure appropriate staffing, resource allocation, and prioritization of quality initiatives to meet operational requirements.
 Build a high-performing quality organization focused on collaboration, continuous improvement, and measurable results.
 Promote employee engagement, knowledge sharing, and the development of future quality leaders.
  
 Performance Monitoring and Business Reporting 
 Establish and maintain effective daily, weekly, and monthly quality performance reviews.
 Monitor key performance indicators, identify unfavorable trends, and ensure timely escalation and resolution of significant quality concerns.
 Communicate quality performance, improvement initiatives, risks, and corrective action progress to plant and business leadership.
 Translate complex quality data into actionable business insights and improvement priorities.
 Ensure quality initiatives are executed within established timelines, budgets, and performance expectations.
  
 Leadership Expectations 
  
 Demonstrate ownership and accountability for manufacturing quality performance.
 Influence decisions and drive results across multiple functions and organizational levels.
 Balance immediate operational quality requirements with long-term strategic improvement objectives.
 Exercise sound judgment in evaluating quality risks, business impacts, and resource priorities.
 Foster collaboration, operational discipline, and continuous improvement.
 Develop organizational capability through effective leadership, talent development, and succession planning.
 
 
 What You'll Bring to Our Team 
 Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related technical discipline; equivalent combination of education and relevant technical experience may be considered.
 Experience in Quality Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Design Engineering, Reliability, Product Service, or a related technical function.
 Demonstrated experience with root cause analysis and structured problem-solving methodologies.
 Ability to analyze technical and quality data and translate findings into actionable recommendations.
 Strong written and verbal communication skills.
 Demonstrated ability to work effectively across multiple functions and organizational levels.
 Ability to manage multiple priorities and technical investigations simultaneously.
 Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel and PowerPoint.
 Knowledge of PFMEA, Control Plans, CAPA, SPC, and other quality systems and tools.
 Experience supporting New Product Introduction and product reliability initiatives.
   
 
 
 Our Culture 
 Our work is centered on our People and Culture as reflected in our Zero Distance philosophy and we recognize the importance of reaffirming our commitment to inclusion and diversity (I&D). This underscores our commitment to fostering an environment where every individual feels valued, connected, and empowered to contribute, while positioning our organization to adapt seamlessly to the evolving needs of our workforce and communities. 

 This reflects our dedication to creating solutions that: Empower colleagues by fostering an environment where all voices are heard, valued, and encouraged to contribute. Strengthen communities where we live and work. Reinforce a culture of belonging, purpose, and engagement. Reflect the diversity of the communities we serve through our workforce, products, and practices. 

 By further embedding Zero Distance into our People and Culture framework, we will continue to build a deeply connected organization. We are cultivating a culture of engagement, belonging, and connection, because while attracting new talent remains a priority, retention is a cornerstone of our strategy. 
 
 
 
 GE Appliances is a trust-based organization. It is important we offer our employees the flexibility they need to do their best work while balancing the needs of the business and individuals. When you join GE Appliances, you will have the opportunity to work with your leader to create a flexible work arrangement that balances the needs of the individual, team, and organization. 
 
 
 GE Appliances is an Equal Opportunity Employer.  Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law. 
 
 GE Appliances participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S 
 
 
 If you are an individual with a disability and need assistance or an accommodation to use our website or to apply, please send an e-mail to ask.recruiting@geappliances.com

This position provides the opportunity to shape the strategy of Eikon’s discovery platform, expand the capabilities of our laboratories, and directly influence the speed and quality of drug discovery.

Executive Director, Automation Operations
As Executive Director of Automation Operations, you will lead the organization that builds, operates, and advances Eikon’s integrated discovery platform.

A near-term mandate is operationalization: moving validated, scientist-developed assay workflows onto the automated platform as production services, with guaranteed turnaround, equivalent or better data quality, and full sample and data traceability.

The platform you will oversee includes integrated systems of liquid handlers (Bravo, Tecan, Hamilton), robotic arms (PF400), automated microscopes (custom in-house imagers, IXMs, etc.), plate readers, incubators, dispensers, Echo acoustic liquid transfer systems, scheduling software, automated compound storage and retrieval systems, and in-house laboratory data systems.

You have stood up laboratory platforms at biotechnology companies before, and you know the difference between automating a workflow and building a platform: the former solves today’s problem, the latter creates capacity for problems no one has posed yet.

You build strong teams, develop managers and senior leaders, set clear priorities across groups with distinct missions, and create an environment of ownership, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
At Elanco (NYSE: ELAN) – it all starts with animals! 
 
 As a global leader in animal health, we are dedicated to innovation and delivering products and services to prevent and treat disease in farm animals and pets. At Elanco, we are driven by our vision of Food and Companionship Enriching Life and our purpose – all to Go Beyond for Animals, Customers, Society and Our People. 
 
 At Elanco, we pride ourselves on fostering a diverse and inclusive work environment. We believe that diversity is the driving force behind innovation, creativity, and overall business success. Here, you’ll be part of a company that values and champions new ways of thinking, work with dynamic individuals, and acquire new skills and experiences that will propel your career to new heights. 
 
 Making animals’ lives better makes life better – join our team today! 
 
 
 The Director, TSMS is responsible for all technical aspects of product and process performance at the Elwood, Kansas monoclonal antibody (mAb) manufacturing facility.  The role is responsible for maintaining and improving the scientific oversight of the manufacturing processes and technical changes, and to ensure the product stewardship across process units and functions.

 In direct collaboration with Manufacturing Operation units and other functions (Quality, Engineering, IT, etc.) the Director, TSMS provides clear direction and the necessary expertise to:
 Ensure the robustness of manufacturing and packaging processes so that all products and processes are maintained in an appropriately validated state of control throughout the product lifecycle. Support and where appropriate lead optimization of biopharmaceutical processes by applying sound scientific reasoning (first principles) and following integrated process and technology strategies. Identify and continuously apply best practices specifically in training, process changes and handling of discrepancy and investigation resolution. Coach and develop TSMS Team members to identify strengths and weaknesses and grow the technical ability of the team.

 Functions, Duties, Tasks :
 Ensure that the technical competencies/knowledge for the site’s monoclonal antibody processes, raw materials, sterile processes, and primary packaging components are in place (as applicable).
 Advises, guides and coaches TSMS associates for the purpose of ensuring routine operational support, identifying solutions and improvement, solving problems, decision making and communication including quality of written reports.
 Ensures adherence to cGMP requirements, guidelines, SOPs, as well as compliance to local laws, the Elanco Red Book, company policies and Health Safety & Environment (HSE) requirements. Particular attention is given to the protection of employees, patients, company assets and the environment.
 Ensure that mAb products and processes are in control and capable, with appropriate control strategies in place to meet Elanco Global Quality and Manufacturing standards and maintain continuity of supply.
 Develop and lead continuous improvement initiatives which positively impact cycle time, productivity, process robustness, gross margin, and production capacity.
 Partner with Commercialization, R&D, Manufacturing, Engineering, Supply Chain and Quality to successfully in-transfer new mAb products.  Ensure that transfers are accomplished on-time, with appropriate process / product control strategies in place.
 Leads cross functional teams for root cause investigations.
 Committed to knowledge sharing/transfer inside site manufacturing groups as well as to Technical R&D (TRD).
 Drives the product control strategy including development and application of KPIs to enable meaningful CPP/CQA trending and reporting of key process data as well as to quickly identify changing quality trends and issues.
 Develop the expense and capital planning budgets for the TSMS function in collaboration with the Sr. Director, Commercialization and site leadership team.  Ensure TSMS delivery meets or exceeds financial commitments.
 Responsible for the design and delivery of TSMS owned technical training programs as well as appropriate technical on-boarding to ensure competency of TSMS associates.
 Stays abreast of technological, regulatory and industry developments, e.g., via internal and external benchmarking.
 Build and grow the TSMS function, recruiting and developing talent in alignment with the site’s strategic needs.
 Maintain a safe work environment and establish a strong safety culture in compliance with Elanco standards and all applicable government requirements.
 Ensure TSMS staff operate in accordance with all applicable Quality and cGMP requirements.  Accountable for quality performance of the function and delivery against site quality targets.
 Develop and review operational objectives with direct reports, establish appropriate talent development plans, and conduct staff performance management reviews as required.
 Other duties as required.
 
 Minimum Qualification (education, experience and/or training, required certifications) :
 Bachelor’s degree in a biomanufacturing related discipline (e.g. biology, Chemistry, engineering, etc.).
 10 years of related working experience
 5+ years’ experience in technical management position.
 5+ years’ experience in (bio)pharmaceutical formulation, process development, or manufacturing technology.
 Ability to lead and develop a team.
 Fundamental understanding of (bio)pharmaceutical analytical testing.
 Demonstrated understanding of Q culture, cGMP standards, and regulatory regulations.
 
 Additional Preferences :
 MSc in Science, Pharmacy, Mechanical or Chemical Engineering, Pharmaceutical Technology.
 Proficiency in applied statistics/Lean Six Sigma methodologies.
 Understanding of USDA, FDA, and EU GMP regulatory standards for veterinary biologics.
 Demonstrated problem solving experience, identifying and understand issues, problems, and opportunities.
 Ability to network and build strong, collaborative relationships across functions / geographies.
 Excellent verbal and written communication skills (English).
 Strong mentoring and coaching skills
 
 Don’t meet every single requirement? Studies have shown underrecognized groups are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single qualification. At Elanco we are dedicated to building a diverse and inclusive work environment. If you think you might be a good fit for a role but don't necessarily meet every single qualification, we encourage you to apply. You may be the right candidate for this role or other roles!

 Elanco Benefits and Perks: 
 We offer a comprehensive benefits package focusing on financial, physical, and mental well-being while encouraging our employees to pursue our purpose! Some highlights include:
 Multiple relocation packages
 8-week parental leave
 9 Employee Resource Groups
 Annual bonus offering
 Flexible work arrangements
 Up to 6% 401K matching

postingQuotes: Plant Manager
The Plant Manager is responsible for the overall leadership, strategic direction, and operational performance of Harbour Industries manufacturing facility.

This role has P&L responsibility for the direct cost drivers of the facility and needs to ensure financial goals are met by managing costs and maximizing revenue generation opportunities, while ensuring best-in-class quality standards.
Partner with Applications and Process Engineering, Quality, and other business functions to implement improvements that reduce waste and scrap, improve yield and quality, and optimize throughput.

Champion and drive a safety-first culture throughout the facility with employee feedback and participation in driving improvement in the safety culture, ensuring compliance with all safety regulations, and implementing and sustaining ongoing safety training and initiatives.

Ensure alignment of production planning, capacity, staffing, and material availability to meet customer and revenue requirements through ownership of Production and collaboration with Planning, Supply Chain, and Sales functions.
Collaborate closely with other departments, including Sales, Engineering, Automation, Data Transformation, HR, and Finance, to align operations with broader organizational goals
We offer a comprehensive benefits package that may include medical, dental, vision, 401k matching, and more!
Mentor team members across all levels to adopt a problem-solving mindset grounded in data-based decisions, curiosity, and shared accountability.

Drive culture of accurate reporting of inventory such as finished good production, scrap, and other future metrics within company’s systems such as Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) and real-time data tracking.

This role oversees all continuous improvement, production, maintenance, and shipping activities while ensuring a world-class safety culture, operational discipline, and alignment to customer, business, and compliance requirements.
Safety & Continuous Improvement
Lead behavior-based safety initiatives, auditing routines, risk identification, root cause investigations, and implementation of corrective/preventive actions.

Collaboration with Quality, Supply Chain, and Process Engineering on root cause investigation, implementing and sustaining corrective actions, and investigating and implementing robust quality control systems to identify and correct defects early in the production process.

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
At El Pollo Loco, we are on a mission to be the nation’s leading fire-grilled chicken restaurant. When it comes to our people, we are all about growth. Whether that means specialized training, a clearly laid out career trajectory or collaborating cross-functionally, we are committed to the success of our people the same way we’ve been committed to the success of the El Pollo Loco brand for the last 50 years. In fact, we see you as our secret ingredient. While our chicken is fire, it’s our people who set us ablaze.
 
 
Our restaurants are only the tip of the flame! If you’re looking for an innovative, winning, and welcoming workplace, then a flamin’ good career in our Restaurant Support Center is right for you.
 
 
At our Support Center, we believe our best work is done Together, when departments collaborate and everyone is confident in contributing their ideas. This is why we are in the office 3 days per week.
 
 
Let’s Get Loco!
 
 
What’s in it for you!
 
 

* STRONG office culture recognized as a Great Place to Work® and driven by our core values: Simple. Together. Relentless. Ownership. Nimble. Growth
* Career growth opportunities
* Competitive pay and bonus potential
* Be an Owner: Equity Compensation
* Medical + Dental + Vision Insurance + HSA Savings Account
* 401(K) Retirement Plan with company match and immediate vesting
* Paid Vacation + Sick Pay + 12 Paid Holidays
* Employee Assistance Program
* Free El Pollo Loco food + restaurant discounts
* PerkSpot discounts program

**POSITION PURPOSE:** 
The Senior Director, Quality Assurance owns El Pollo Loco's enterprise quality assurance function end to end, consolidating vendor-level quality assurance and regulatory food safety compliance into a single point of accountability. This role is responsible for the integrity of the supply chain's quality systems — from supplier and co-manufacturer qualification through regulatory compliance across federal, state, and local agencies — and serves as the primary quality and food safety resource to the franchise system.
 
 
**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:** 
Vendor & Supplier Quality Assurance
 

* Directs vendor and supplier quality assurance programs across El Pollo Loco's poultry portfolio, including fresh leg quarters (“Saddles”) and value-added further-processed chicken items, ensuring specification integrity, ingredient consistency, and product quality at every stage of the supply chain.
* Leads vendor qualification, audit, scorecarding, and corrective-action programs; partners with Procurement and Distribution to resolve quality holds, non-conformances, and supplier performance issues.
* Owns quality specifications for co-manufactured and further-processed chicken products, working directly with processors to validate manufacturing controls, shelf-life, and food safety design prior to system-wide rollout.
* Evaluates and approves new vendors, ingredients, and product formulations, ensuring alignment with brand quality standards and regulatory requirements.

Regulatory & Food Safety Compliance
 

* Serves as the company's senior point of accountability for food safety regulatory compliance, including FDA, USDA, FSMA, HACCP, GFSI, and state and local health department requirements across all operating jurisdictions.
* Builds and maintains direct working relationships with state and federal regulatory agencies; leads the company's response to regulatory inquiries, inspections, and enforcement actions.
* Owns crisis management, product withdrawal, and recall protocols (including activation of the Level 3 Withdrawal Process), partnering with executive leadership and legal counsel as needed.
* Directs internal and third-party food safety audit programs spanning restaurants, distribution centers, and manufacturing partners.

Team Leadership & Franchise Support
 

* Builds, leads, and develops a high-performing QA organization spanning both vendor quality and regulatory food safety disciplines; sets performance expectations, coaching plans, and succession pipelines for direct reports.
* Serves as a critical QA partner to the franchise system, delivering training, technical guidance, and responsive support to franchisees on quality and food safety matters.
* Represents Quality Assurance in cross-functional and executive leadership forums, translating vendor and regulatory risk into clear, actionable guidance for Operations and senior leadership.
* Other duties as assigned by the SVP, Supply Chain & Quality Assurance.

QUALIFICATIONS – EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE, LICENSE/CERTIFICATIONS:
 
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to satisfactorily perform the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodation will be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job. The requirements listed below are representative of the education and/or experience required.
 
 
**Education/Work Experience:** 
BA/BS in Food Science, Food Microbiology, or a related field required; Master's degree preferred. Minimum 12+ years of progressive quality assurance and food safety experience, with substantial, direct experience in poultry and value-added/further-processed chicken products required. Demonstrated background working directly with state and federal regulatory agencies (FDA, USDA, state health departments) on compliance, inspections, or enforcement matters required. Prior experience directly managing and developing a quality assurance team required.
 
 
**License/Certifications:** 
Valid driver's license required. HACCP certification required; PCQI (Preventive Controls Qualified Individual) preferred.
 
 
**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:** 

* Proven track record building, managing, and developing high-performing quality assurance teams, with strong people-leadership, coaching, and succession-planning skills.
* Deep working knowledge of value-added and further-processed chicken manufacturing, including co-manufacturer oversight, specification management, and shelf-life validation.
* Established credibility with state and federal regulatory agencies; skilled at navigating inspections, audits, and enforcement proceedings with composure and precision.
* Demonstrated ability to support and train franchisees on quality and food safety standards, balancing brand protection with practical, field-level guidance.
* Confidence in execution of strategic initiatives; decisive and able to make fact-based decisions under pressure.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving mindset and skills; meticulous attention to detail.
* Ability to effectively communicate with internal and external business partners, including vendors, regulators, and franchisees.
* Ability to prioritize and plan competing, time-sensitive work assignments under frequent, tight deadlines.
* Ability to read, write, and interpret complex regulatory reports, contracts, and correspondence.
* Ability to exercise independent judgment on matters of significant risk and consequence to the company.
* Ability to work weekends and extended work schedules as needed.
* Willing and able to travel locally within Southern California and to out-of-state vendor, distribution, and restaurant locations, as needed, by car or airplane.

Our Company
 
 
In 1980 the first American El Pollo Loco opened on Alvarado Street in Los Angeles, quickly becoming a destination for the best citrus-marinated, fire-grilled pollo in town. Over the past four decades, El Pollo Loco has grown into more than 500 restaurants across 9 states, becoming an L.A. mainstay and cultural benchmark along the way. Today, we continue to work just as hard to always provide our customers with Quality Chicken. Fast. Easy. Affordable.
 
 
PAY DISCLAIMER – CA ONLY

This range does not include any benefits or bonus opportunities that might be available for the position based on position and eligibility criteria. At El Pollo Loco, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at the high end of the range. Individual pay decisions will vary based on a variety of factors including years of experience, industry experience, education, geography, etc.

postingQuotes: Working closely with internal stakeholders and CMOs, this role provides technical and operational leadership across the ARS outsourced manufacturing network.

Responsibilities include leading Technical Operations projects, supporting formulation and process development, technology transfer, GMP manufacturing activities, and resolution of technical and operational issues.

* Manage cross-functional Technical Operations projects and day-to-day technical and operational interactions with assigned external partners, including scope, timelines, deliverables, responsibilities, budgets, risks, key milestones, project meetings, action tracking, scopes of work, proposals, change orders, and CMO/vendor performance metrics and KPIs (e.g., service, quality, delivery, capacity, and right-first-time).

* Plan and support clinical and commercial manufacturing campaigns in coordination with CMOs, Supply Chain, Quality Assurance, and other internal functions; provide on-site/person-in-plant support for key manufacturing activities as needed.
* Experience with drug-device combination products, nasal/inhalation products, sterile manufacturing, commercial product launch, or PPQ is preferred.

* Demonstrated technical understanding of formulation, manufacturing processes, scale-up, technology transfer, process validation, and process performance sufficient to critically evaluate CMO data and recommendations, work effectively in cross-functional technical teams, and hold external partners accountable to commitments.
*This position is also eligible for Equity, 401k matching, and our excellent benefits package including 100% employer paid Medical, Dental & Vision for employees.

* Review manufacturing and process documentation, including master and executed batch records, protocols, reports, process performance data, vendor change controls, investigations, and annual/product reviews, for technical accuracy and process performance.
* Monitor and trend manufacturing and process performance data to identify emerging risks, process drift, and opportunities for continuous improvement and operational excellence.
* Monitor and trend manufacturing and process performance data to identify emerging risks, process drift, and opportunities for continuous improvement and operational excellence.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office and project/reporting tools; experience with project management, continuous improvement, or operational excellence methodologies is a plus.

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
**Position Purpose:**
 
Lead and direct process improvement activities that provide more efficient and streamlined workflow. 
**Key Details:** Must reside in Indiana or be willing to relocate to Indiana.

 

* Responsible for leading and collaborating with others on National Committee for Quality Assurance (NCQA) Accreditation and/or Healthcare Effectiveness Data and Information Set (HEDIS) performance

 

* Responsible for quality improvement aspects of risk adjustment processes for all products

 

* Collaborate with Medicare STARS team to improve overall STARS ratings for Medicare products (including HEDIS, CAHPS, HOS)

 

* Oversee provider satisfaction surveys and implement action plans for improvements

 

* Research and incorporate best practices into operations

 

* Organize and control activities, methods, and procedures to achieve business objectives

 

* Review and implement new technological tools and processes and fosters team concept with internal and external constituencies

 

* Present results of improvement efforts and ongoing performance measures to senior management

 

* Formulate and establish policies, operating procedures, and goals in compliance with internal and external guidelines

 

* Collaborate with State, County, and local agencies to promote services that improve health outcomes, decrease health disparities and reduce the cost of care.

 

* Work closely with State, County and local agencies, community stakeholders and communities to monitor the application of all standards

 

* Promote an environment of cultural competence throughout the health plan through identification and implementation of culturally-inclusive best practices and innovations, such as the development of provider trainings to improve cultural awareness and competency within the provider network

 

* Oversee the assessment of cultural diversity of the provider network to identify resources and gaps, including needs analysis for non-traditional providers (traditional healers, religious and spiritual resources, natural support systems, etc.) and develops recommendations for credentialing and network development activities.

 

* Monitor and evaluate provider practices through KPIs within health equity dashboards to assess and improve the cultural competence of delivered services by addressing care gaps and aligning interventions to resolve.

 

* Oversee the population specific activities (such as training, awareness through the media, and partnering with various external equity stakeholders), including cultural treatment teams and other cultural community support system activities.

 

* Oversee the comprehensive, outcomes-based Cultural Competency Plan that is aligned with CLAS standards and national and regional priorities/initiatives.

 

* The plan also incorporates data-driven assessments of culturally competent performance, and defines a strategy for the continual provision, monitoring and improvement of culturally competent performance.

 

* Manage outreach budget for Cultural Competency programs and sponsorships.
* Performs other duties as assigned.

 

* Complies with all policies and standards.

**Education/Experience:**
 
 
Bachelor's Degree Nursing, other related field or equivalent experience required 
 
**Master's Degree preferred:**

7+ years of quality management, quality improvement or healthcare operations experience required 
 
**Licenses/Certifications:**
 
 
Certain states may require a formal certification in quality improvement, risk management, or another parallel field. 
Current state’s RN license preferred 
 
**Certified Professional in Health Care Quality preferred**

Pay Range: $107,700.00 - $199,300.00 per year

**At Centene, we connect people to the care they need to live healthier lives — and the work you do here makes that impact real every day.** You’ll take on meaningful challenges that directly support individuals, families, and communities, building your skills while making healthcare more accessible and effective. It’s work with a purpose you can see, backed by a team committed to improving lives well beyond the workday.

Centene offers a comprehensive benefits package including: competitive pay, health insurance, 401K and stock purchase plans, tuition reimbursement, paid time off plus holidays, and a flexible approach to work with remote, hybrid, field or office work schedules. Actual pay will be adjusted based on an individual's skills, experience, education, and other job-related factors permitted by law, including full-time or part-time status. Total compensation may also include additional forms of incentives. Benefits may be subject to program eligibility.

Centene is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, and values the ways in which we are different. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered in accordance with the LA County Ordinance and the California Fair Chance Act

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE TEAM

 Frontier Systems (AFS) is focused on positioning Anduril as a lead provider of specialized hardware and software products for defense, law enforcement, and intelligence customers. We work alongside our customers to understand their requirements and deliver exquisite capabilities across their problem set. We aim to develop and deploy critically needed capabilities that address our customers' most pressing national security requirements.

Product Operations is the team accountable for the health of the systems and technology that delivers the capabilities that our customers depend on. The function identifies, triages, and drives resolution of incidents across the deployed fleet, and converts what we've learned into the reliability and sustainment insights that product and engineering teams act upon. We work in close coordination with product engineering, reliability, quality, program management, and field operations teams to maximize capability availability for our end users and inform the next cycle of iterations.

 ABOUT THE ROLE

 As the Senior Manager of Product Operations for Frontier Systems, you will own product operations across the division's product portfolio and the programs that deliver those products. You will lead multiple Product Operations managers, each of whom runs a team of technical specialists and engineers focused on supporting and improving fielded products. The division's portfolio is scaling, and this role exists to scale support alongside it, both for the products the function covers today and for the ones that reach the field next.

This is a function maturation and growth role as much as an operating one, and the work rewards depth. The position requires a strong problem-solving mindset, enough technical depth to follow the work of the engineers and specialists supporting fielded robotic systems, and the judgment to make decisions whose impact reaches beyond your own team and the current planning cycle. If you are passionate about cutting-edge technology, advancing national security, and delivering best-in-class operational support, Anduril invites you to join the team.

 WHAT YOU'LL DO

 Lead and Grow the Function: Lead Product Operations across the Frontier Systems portfolio, managing multiple teams and driving the growth of both sustainment capability and resourcing across the division. Own hiring, performance, development, and organizational design, while also maturing the function itself: the operating model, the standards, and the capability of the people in it.

 Own Service Quality, Internal and External: Hold accountability for the quality of product support delivered to external customers and to internal Anduril teams. Understand the work at every level, both how it is expected to be done and how it is actually being done, and close the distance between the two.

 Scale Support Operations Across the Portfolio: Think strategically about how support scales across the division's full portfolio, current and future. Extend Product Operations coverage to new products and programs as they reach fielded maturity, standing up scope, coverage, escalation paths, and support infrastructure where none exists. All while holding service quality steady as the fielded population grows.

 Align Capacity to Demand: Align support headcount demand to measured support volume, fielded asset population, and product delivery schedules. Own annual headcount planning for the function and produce defensible demand calculations when planning cycles call for them.

 Own the Failure Signal and the fielded product Reliability Loop: Own the workflow that converts field failures into structured, trustworthy signal for product and reliability engineering, spanning failure mode classification, root cause corrective action cycle performance, and recurrence measurement. Partner with engineering to abstract individual incidents into systemic improvements, holding engineering partners accountable to the signal provided and your own organization accountable to its fidelity.

 Set the Support and Sustainment Standard: Establish and enforce the standards by which the organization triages, diagnoses, escalates, and resolves product incidents, including the severity discipline that determines what reaches engineering and when. Mature the sustainment approach for complex electromechanical products supporting the evolution of maintenance, spares and hardware action, configuration and calibration management, and the self-service and tooling investments that reduce support burden over time.

 Sponsor Function Initiatives: Outline and sponsor the initiatives that mature the function, defining the end state, the measure of success, and the resourcing. Then hold program management partners accountable for leading and delivering the targeted outcomes. 

 Be the Interface for Support Requirements: Serve as the point of contact program teams come to when assessing product and customer service support requirements for new and expanding programs. Characterize the cost of the service and define the contract and pricing structures that fund it, in support of proposals and modifications.

 Brief Executive Stakeholders: Represent product support to business line and division leadership through recurring reviews of fleet health, reliability trends, sustainment cost, and the maturation of the service. Surface systemic problems with evidence, drive cross-functional prioritization, and help deeply technical teams, program stakeholders, and operators in the field understand each other.

 Travel and Availability: Ability to travel up to 20% to support customer needs and operations, and to work non-standard hours when fielded operations require it.

 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 
 Proven Technical Leadership: 8+ years of professional experience managing, mastering, and supporting complex technical systems (robotics, aerospace, defense, automotive, or other electromechanical domains).

 Education: Bachelor's degree in a technical or related field, OR equivalent hands-on technical experience (military, industrial, or field support).

 Organizational Leadership: Experience leading managers and multi-team organizations, with accountability for outcomes across more than one product line or program.

 Incident Workflow Ownership: Experience owning incident-driven workflows at a standard-setting level, including triage, diagnosis, severity assignment, escalation, and resolution across a fielded fleet.

 Technical Depth: Enough technical depth to follow the work of engineers and specialists supporting fielded robotic and electromechanical systems, including the ability to reason across hardware, software, and networking boundaries.

 Reliability Workflow Familiarity: Demonstrated familiarity with product improvement or reliability lifecycles and processes.

 Sustainment Approach: Experience defining a sustainment model for fielded hardware across its service life, spanning maintenance, spares, and the tooling or self-service investments that reduce support burden.

 Capacity and Cost Modeling: Experience building and defending quantitative models that size support demand, headcount, or cost, including owning annual planning for a function and stating the assumptions behind the model.

 Program Management: Project and program management ability applied outside a project management role: decomposing requirements into deliverables, synthesizing information from several sources into a clear recommendation, and driving that recommendation to a result across multiple functions.

 Executive Influence: Proven ability to align senior cross-functional leadership and influence outcomes without authority over the people who deliver them, including briefing executive stakeholders on operational performance.

 Communication: Excellent written, visual, and verbal communication skills, and confidence navigating ambiguity and establishing new ways of working where none exist.

 Clearance: Active or eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret Security clearance. Holding clearances or background investigations in the past is a plus.

 
 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 We recognize that great leaders come from diverse backgrounds. We do not expect you to meet every single one of these criteria:

 
 Experience establishing a product support or sustainment function from the ground up, including defining the operating model, growing the team, and running remote support operations for complex robotics systems.

 Defense, law enforcement, or other government agency experience leading air defense, intelligence, and/or force protection teams.

 Consulting or process maturation project experience, and formal training or certification in a continuous improvement or project management disciplines (such as Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, Agile, or PMP).

 Fluency with structured root cause methods such as fault tree analysis, fishbone, or 8D problem solving.

 Working knowledge of reliability engineering fundamentals, including failure distributions, mean time between failure and maintenance, and reliability growth.

 Hands-on exposure to the failure behavior of fielded robotic and sensor systems, including actuation, power systems, sensing, embedded compute, radar, RF detection, and electro-optical and infrared sensing, and the ability to diagnose connectivity and networking faults across distributed field systems.

 Comfort reading logs, telemetry, and test data, including hands-on use of Linux command-line interfaces and tooling such as Grafana, Datadog, Jira, Git, SQL, and Palantir Foundry.

 Experience translating support scope into contract or pricing structures for operations and sustainment, and familiarity with proposal efforts.

 Fluency with the data layer of sustainment, including incident management systems, asset and configuration data, service bill of materials, and cost association.

 Experience in on-call support operations and limited risk tolerance environments.

 An active U.S. Secret clearance or higher, prior military service, or a defense and STEM background.

 US Salary Range
 $147,000 — $196,000 USD 


 The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including: 

 

 Benefits 

 At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits . 

 

 
 Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams 

 Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.



 
 To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

 
 
 No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.



 Please always verify communications: 
 
 Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.

 Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com . 

 


 
 Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.



 
 What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com . Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.



 


 

 Data Privacy

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
**We believe power is a promise - a shared commitment to be there for others when it matters most.**
====================================================================================================

For more than 65 years, we've turned big ideas into solutions that help protect homes, strengthen businesses and build a more resilient, efficient, sustainable energy future.

Ready to Power a Smarter World with us?

Generac Home is hiring a Senior Manager, Manufacturing Test Engineering. In this role you will lead Manufacturing Test organization responsible for manufacturing test strategy, automated test equipment, test software development, production data systems, engineering laboratories, and factory test deployment. This leader will be primarily working on Home product portfolio that involves our Solar & Storage, Interconnect Controls & PowerGen products.

You will lead and manage a multidisciplinary team of software developers, test engineers, designers, and technicians supporting PCBA Functional Test, End-of-Line (EOL) Test, Safety Test, and Run-In/Burn-In systems across internal and contract manufacturing sites.

Preferred location: Reno NV, (Santa Moncia OR Waukesha WI as options)

**Essential Responsibilities:**

**Team Leadership**

* Lead and develop a team of manufacturing test engineers, software developers, and designers.
* Establish organization strategy, technical roadmaps, staffing plans, and annual objectives.
* Manage departmental budgets, capital investments, contractors, and external suppliers.
* Drive a culture of technical excellence, innovation, safety, and continuous improvement.

**Manufacturing Test Engineering**

* Define manufacturing test strategies for power electronics, energy storage, controls, and Clean Energy products.
* Lead development and deployment of PCBA Functional Test, End-of-Line Test, HiPot/Safety Test, and Run-In/Burn-In systems.
* Establish standardized test architectures, specifications, coverage requirements, and deployment processes.
* Support factory launches, production ramp-ups, and test-system transfers across manufacturing sites.

* Lead development of manufacturing test software and automation solutions.
* Oversee applications utilizing Golang, Python, C#, LabVIEW, Linux, PLCs, and industrial automation technologies.
* Ensure integration of test systems with MES, databases, traceability systems, and manufacturing infrastructure.
* Improve test coverage, uptime, first-pass yield, cycle time, and diagnostic capabilities through automation and software innovation.

**Data Analytics & Traceability**

* Lead development of manufacturing test dashboards, data pipelines, and analytics platforms.
* Drive use of ClickHouse, Grafana, Power BI, and other tools for yield, throughput, failure analysis, and factory performance monitoring.
* Establish data-driven approaches for root cause analysis, quality improvement, and production optimization.

**Cross-Functional Leadership**

* Partner with Product Engineering, Firmware, Manufacturing, Quality, Reliability, Operations, and Supply Chain teams.
* Drive Design-for-Test (DFT) initiatives and manufacturing test readiness for new products.
* Lead manufacturing test support at internal factories and contract manufacturers globally

**Minimum Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering; Electrical, Computer Science, or related technical discipline.
* 10+ years of engineering experience in manufacturing test, automation, software development, or electronics manufacturing.
* 5+ years of engineering leadership experience.
* Experience with automated test equipment, production software, and high-volume manufacturing environments.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with energy storage, power electronics, inverters, or embedded systems.
* Experience with Golang, Python, C#, LabVIEW, Linux, SQL databases, and industrial communication protocols.
* Experience with SIL/HIL systems, automated test equipment, and production analytics platforms.
* Experience supporting NPI and contract manufacturing operations.
* Familiarity with CAN, Ethernet, RS-232, RS-485, and other embedded communication protocols.

No 3rd parties or agencies at this time.

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
### **The Position**

From the beginning, Genentech has been a team of highly dedicated, passionate individuals. We are a place where people are united around a single purpose and an ambitious vision. Together, we aspire to deliver ever better health outcomes for patients while lowering overall healthcare costs. Our goal is to compel the customer to act on behalf of their patients while showing great commitment to the rare disease community, whose support is key. Utilizing innovative methods to identify patients who may benefit from treatment, we must take a highly strategic approach to patient access while assisting patients and their caregivers to navigate the healthcare system.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Field Operations Director serves as the trusted operations partner to an assigned Regional VP or National Team VP and their leadership team, helping translate business priorities into clear plans, coordinated execution, and effective connection to the broader CE Operations and enterprise support network. The Director owns the operating rhythm and priority agenda for the assigned leadership team and provides a single point of connectivity between Field Leadership and the broader operational ecosystem.

SCOPE & KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Strategic Partnership with Field Leadership

* Serve as the primary Operations partner to an assigned Regional VP or National Team VP and their leadership team.
* Develop a deep understanding of the team's business priorities, customers, opportunities, challenges, and performance.
* Translate enterprise and CE priorities into clear implications and action plans for the assigned Region or National Team.
* Provide strategic and operational counsel to leadership and proactively identify issues requiring attention, decisions, or escalation.
* Help leadership prioritize competing needs and maintain focus on the highest-impact business opportunities.

Operating Rhythm & Business Planning

* Own the operating rhythm and priority agenda for the assigned leadership team.
* Lead development and coordination of annual, quarterly, and other operating plans.
* Translate priorities into clear roadmaps with owners, milestones, dependencies, and measures of progress.
* Coordinate leadership agendas, decision materials, action tracking, and follow-through.
* Support Regional or National Team input into ABP, resource planning, RBO, and other CE and enterprise planning processes.

Operational Integration & Execution

* Serve as a front door for operational requests from the assigned leadership team and route needs to the appropriate CE Operations or enterprise partner.
* Connect Field Leadership and HEDs to the broader support network without requiring them to independently navigate multiple teams.
* Coordinate across Enterprise Operations, RBO, Squad Field Partners, ABP, DDA, L&SD, and other functions to enable execution.
* Anticipate execution barriers, dependencies, and operational risks and mobilize partners to resolve them.
* Ensure appropriate communication and coordination between enterprise initiatives and Regional/National execution.

Insights & Decision Support

* Synthesize field insights, performance signals, customer information, and emerging business needs into clear leadership implications.
* Develop business reviews and decision materials that enable productive leadership conversations.
* Identify patterns and recurring needs that may have implications beyond the assigned Region or National Team.
* Surface cross-field opportunities, risks, and common needs to the Head of CE Field Operations so they can be addressed across the organization where appropriate.
* Provide recommendations related to priorities, resources, capacity, and operational tradeoffs.

Resource & Capacity Planning

* Maintain an integrated understanding of the assigned team's resource and capacity requirements.
* Support Regional or National Team roster, resource, and capacity planning.
* Identify capacity constraints and emerging needs and develop recommendations in partnership with Field Leadership.
* Connect local resource needs to broader CE and enterprise planning processes.

KEY DELIVERABLES

* Annual and quarterly operating plans
* Regional or National Team priority roadmap
* Leadership agendas, decision materials, and action logs
* Business reviews and synthesized field insights
* RBO, ABP, and enterprise planning inputs
* Resource, roster, and capacity plans
* Consolidated requests, risks, and capacity recommendations
* Clear escalation of cross-field opportunities and common operational needs

MINDSET & CAPABILITIES

* Trusted partner who builds credibility with senior Field Leaders
* Strategic thinker with strong operational discipline
* Able to translate ambiguity and complexity into clear plans and actions
* Strong business acumen and understanding of field execution
* Highly effective at influencing without formal authority
* Skilled at connecting people, priorities, and resources across organizational boundaries
* Strong analytical and synthesis capabilities
* Proactive and anticipatory rather than reactive
* Comfortable navigating a complex, matrixed environment
* Strong judgment and ability to distinguish between issues that should be solved locally and those requiring enterprise solutions
* Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining focus on business impact
* Growth mindset and commitment to continuous improvement

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

* Bachelor's degree required
* Significant pharmaceutical, biotechnology, consulting, commercial, field operations, strategic, and/or analytical experience (8+ years preferred)
* Demonstrated experience partnering with senior business or field leaders
* Experience translating strategy into operational plans and driving execution
* Strong project/program management and cross-functional leadership capabilities
* Demonstrated ability to operate effectively within a complex matrixed organization
* Strong communication, executive presentation, analytical, and problem-solving skills
* Ability and willingness to travel as required for internal and external business meetings

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

* Graduate-level degree (e.g., MBA or advanced life sciences degree)
* Prior Field, Field Operations, Commercial Operations, or business planning experience
* Experience with resource planning, business planning, account planning, or field effectiveness
* Experience supporting Regional or National field leadership teams

Location: This is a Field-based role and relocation benefits are not available.

The expected salary range for this position based on the primary location of CA is $147,900 - $274,700 USD Annual. Actual pay will be determined based on experience, qualifications, geographic location, and other job-related factors permitted by law. A discretionary annual bonus may be available based on individual and Company performance. This position also qualifies for the benefits detailed at the link provided below.

*Benefits*

Genentech is an equal opportunity employer. It is our policy and practice to employ, promote, and otherwise treat any and all employees and applicants on the basis of merit, qualifications, and competence. The company's policy prohibits unlawful discrimination, including but not limited to, discrimination on the basis of Protected Veteran status, individuals with disabilities status, and consistent with all federal, state, or local laws.

If you have a disability and need an accommodation in relation to the online application process, please contact us by completing this form Accommodations for Applicants.
