record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
Airlite Plastics is a premier, privately held, family-owned manufacturer headquartered in Omaha, Nebraska. Our family style and personal culture is what makes Airlite an amazing place to grow and build a successful career. Airlite’s company values of unquestionable integrity and respect and appreciation for each other are at the core of our success! These values set a strong foundation to build on where we can ‘wow’ our customers with innovative products and sustainable solutions and continuously improve our processes and efficiencies.

 

Our product lines include rigid plastic containers and lids for food packaging and cosmetics, dry powder scoops, plastic drink cups, shipping containers, industrial strength insulated concrete forms (ICF) and sustainable permeable paving systems. As pioneers in our industry, focused on sustainable solutions, we strive to provide our customers with top-notch service and quality, which aligns with our award-winning products.

 

As Airlite continues to grow and expand, we are excited to add new roles across our organization to support increasing customer demand and future innovation. This is an exciting time to join our team and be part of a company investing in people, technology, and long-term success.

 

**How would you contribute?**

This role is a contributing member of our team located in Nazareth, PA. As a Director of Operations you are a key to continued growth and success of Airlite. The Director of Operations provides strategic and operational leadership for manufacturing operations across assigned Airlite Locations. This role is responsible for Production, Maintenance, and Engineering and ensures operational strategies, resources, and priorities are aligned with business objectives.

This role will drive operational excellence through strong leadership, development of site leadership teams, continuous improvement, effective use of performance metrics, and disciplined execution. A key focus of this position is building leadership capability throughout the organization by coaching and developing managers and supervisors as the operations continue to grow and evolve. The Director will balance consistent operational expectations across locations while recognizing the unique needs and autonomy of each facility.

**Essential Duties:**

* Provide strategic leadership and direction for Production, Maintenance, and Engineering across the Nazareth and Lakeville facilities.

* Lead, coach, and develop operational leaders, strengthening leadership capability, accountability, decision-making, and succession readiness throughout the organization.

* Establish operational priorities, goals, and KPIs and use performance data to drive accountability and continuous improvement.

* Ensure manufacturing operations consistently achieve objectives related to safety, quality, delivery, productivity, efficiency, and cost.

* Partner with site leadership to develop and execute operational plans that support business growth, capacity requirements, equipment needs, and organizational objectives.

* Drive continuous improvement initiatives that improve manufacturing processes, equipment reliability, labor effectiveness, throughput, and overall operational performance.

* Provide leadership for capital projects, equipment installations, process improvements, and other operational initiatives in partnership with Engineering and Maintenance.

* Evaluate organizational structure, staffing, and leadership needs and develop teams capable of supporting current operations and future growth.

* Promote consistency and sharing of best practices between facilities while allowing each operation to respond effectively to its specific business and manufacturing needs.

* Partner cross-functionally with Quality, Supply Chain, Safety, Human Resources, Finance, Sales, Customer Service, and other functions to resolve issues and achieve business objectives.

* Develop and manage operational budgets, forecasts, capital requirements, and resource plans in alignment with financial and strategic objectives.

* Foster a culture of safety, accountability, collaboration, employee development, continuous improvement, and operational excellence while exemplifying Airlite's Core Values and servant leadership principles.

* Other duties as assigned.

 

**Do you have what it takes?** Airlite Plastics is a versatile employer; complacency is not one of our strengths! We work hard each day to ensure that equipment efficiency and customer satisfaction never leave our line of sight. Successful candidates for the role will possess the following:

 

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, Operations Management, Manufacturing, or a related field preferred; equivalent combination of education and relevant experience may be considered.
* 10+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, including significant responsibility for manufacturing operations.
* 5+ years of experience leading managers and/or senior operational leaders.
* Demonstrated experience overseeing multiple operational functions such as Production, Maintenance, and Engineering.
* Experience leading operations across multiple facilities or business units strongly preferred.
* Experience with capital planning, operational budgeting, continuous improvement, and manufacturing performance management.
* Plastics manufacturing, injection molding, extrusion, or related manufacturing experience preferred.
* Demonstrated ability to coach, mentor, and develop managers and emerging leaders.
* Strong business and financial acumen with the ability to understand the impact of operational decisions on overall business performance.
* Ability to effectively lead across multiple facilities, balancing consistent operational expectations with the unique needs of each location.
* Capability to solve complex problems, utilizing strong critical thinking and decision-making skills
* Superior organizational skills and the ability to assemble resources needed to orchestrate multiple projects/activities and accomplish goals
* Model a collaborative leadership style with the ability to build partnerships and influence others into action
* Excellent verbal and written communications skills
* Outstanding presentation and facilitation skills
* Excellent interpersonal skills and consultative approach; tactful in dealing with people at all levels
* Strong sense of urgency, self-motivated and positive
* Flexible and adaptable; able to work in ambiguous situations
* Ability to actively lead change initiatives
* Display highest ethical standards
* Maintain the utmost level of confidentiality in dealing with sensitive information
* Detail oriented, with the ability to multi-task in a fast-paced environment

 

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit; stand; walk; use hand dexterity to operate office equipment including computer keyboards; reach with hands and arms; and talk and hear. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 15 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee may be exposed to moving mechanical parts. The noise level in the office work environment is typically quiet; when visiting the production floor, the noise level may be loud.

 

**Our Core Values Drive Us!**

 

* Do you conduct yourself with unquestionable integrity?

* Do you demonstrate respect and appreciation for those around you?

* Are you innovative and strive to challenge the status quo?

* Do you strive for continuous improvement and to deliver the “wow” factor?

* Do you care about environmentally sustainable solutions?

* Do you take meaning and pride in a job well done?

 

**What’s in it for you?** ***As a Full-Time employee, you will be eligible for the following benefits:***

 

* Health, dental and vision insurance

* Company paid life insurance

* Company paid short term disability

* Generous 401k match

* Generous Time Off

* Annual company activities

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
**JOB DESCRIPTION** 
 
 

Step into a leadership role, where your management skills will drive strategic risk and compliance initiatives. Embrace the opportunity to enhance your leadership capabilities and make a meaningful impact on the future of risk management and control testing. 
 
As a **Compliance and Operations Risk Test Director** in the Testing Center of Excellence, you will play a pivotal role in shaping the testing strategy across various business lines, ensuring alignment with regulatory and firm requirements. Your expertise in risk management and control testing will be instrumental in identifying and mitigating risks, thereby enhancing compliance and operational risk management. You will be expected to make independent decisions that significantly impact operations and financial management, while also leading large teams and managing service delivery. Your proficiency in problem-solving, decision-making, and resource optimization will be key in driving results that accelerate our business objectives. Your role will also involve fostering strong relationships with stakeholders, interpreting regulatory requirements, and effectively communicating risk reports to various management levels. 
 
**Job responsibilities**

* Lead the development and implementation of comprehensive testing strategies across various business lines, ensuring alignment with regulatory and firm requirements.
* Oversee complex testing initiatives, utilizing advanced knowledge in risk management and control testing to identify and mitigate unmitigated risks.
* Make independent, strategic decisions that significantly impact operations, financial management, and compliance, based on in-depth analysis and expert judgment.
* Foster strong relationships with senior stakeholders, interpreting regulatory requirements and effectively communicating risk reports to various management levels.
* Manage large teams, setting professional standards, and ensuring efficient service delivery, while also contributing to the longer-term plans for the area to fit within broader functional and organization strategy.

**Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills**

* 10 years of experience in leading and implementing comprehensive testing strategies in a financial institution.
* Proven track record in managing large teams, setting professional standards, and ensuring efficient service delivery.
* Demonstrated expertise in interpreting and applying regulatory requirements within the context of risk management and control testing.
* Advanced proficiency in utilizing risk dashboards to provide SMART risk reporting, communications, and presentations for various forums and management levels.
* Expertise in resource optimization, with a focus on efficiently leveraging allocated people, money, and technologies to plan, schedule, and progress project and program initiatives.

**ABOUT US** 
 
 

JPMorganChase, one of the oldest financial institutions, offers innovative financial solutions to millions of consumers, small businesses and many of the world's most prominent corporate, institutional and government clients under the J.P. Morgan and Chase brands. Our history spans over 200 years and today we are a leader in investment banking, consumer and small business banking, commercial banking, financial transaction processing and asset management.

We offer a competitive total rewards package including base salary determined based on the role, experience, skill set and location. Those in eligible roles may receive commission-based pay and/or discretionary incentive compensation, paid in the form of cash and/or forfeitable equity, awarded in recognition of individual achievements and contributions. We also offer a range of benefits and programs to meet employee needs, based on eligibility. These benefits include comprehensive health care coverage, on-site health and wellness centers, a retirement savings plan, backup childcare, tuition reimbursement, mental health support, financial coaching and more. Additional details about total compensation and benefits will be provided during the hiring process.

We recognize that our people are our strength and the diverse talents they bring to our global workforce are directly linked to our success. We are an equal opportunity employer and place a high value on diversity and inclusion at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of any protected attribute, including race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital or veteran status, pregnancy or disability, or any other basis protected under applicable law. We also make reasonable accommodations for applicants' and employees' religious practices and beliefs, as well as mental health or physical disability needs. Visit our FAQs for more information about requesting an accommodation.

JPMorgan Chase & Co. is an Equal Opportunity Employer, including Disability/Veterans

 
 
**ABOUT THE TEAM** 
 
 

Our professionals in our Corporate Functions cover a diverse range of areas from finance and risk to human resources and marketing. Our corporate teams are an essential part of our company, ensuring that we're setting our businesses, clients, customers and employees up for success.

 

Control Management maintains a strong and consistent control environment through a joint accountability model that aligns managers with each function and region to mitigate operational risk. The team focuses on four areas: Control Design & Expertise, Risks & Controls Identification/Assessment, Issues & Control Deficiencies and Control Governance & Reporting.

**Market Director of Operations**

**Coverage Area: Kansas (KC, Laurence, Overland Park) and Iowa (Davenport and Des Moines)**

**Job Summary**

The Market Director is a key operational leader responsible for the performance of a geographic network of BHG treatment centers. This role directly leads and develops Program Directors and, through those leaders, is accountable for the operational, clinical, financial, and team performance of each treatment center within the market.

This is an opportunity for an experienced multi-site healthcare leader who enjoys developing people, improving performance, solving complex operational challenges, and expanding access to high-quality patient care.

The Market Director is accountable for building a high-performing market that delivers exceptional patient care, operational excellence, strong leadership, and sustainable growth. The Market Director will also perform duties within the scope of their license or certification when applicable, as outlined in an addendum to this job description.

**What You’ll Be Accountable For**

As Market Director, you will:

* Build high-performing leaders and create a culture of accountability.
* Deliver strong operational execution and financial performance.
* Ensure outstanding patient outcomes and timely access to care.
* Maintain regulatory excellence and operational integrity.
* Drive sustainable growth through referrals and community engagement.

**Key Areas of Responsibility**

**Leadership Development**

* Mentor, coach, and develop high-performing Program Directors and other market leaders.
* Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
Who we are 
 With its A.I.-powered robotic technology platform, Symbotic is changing the way consumer goods move through the supply chain. Intelligent software orchestrates advanced robots in a high-density, end-to-end system – reinventing warehouse automation for increased efficiency, speed and flexibility. 
 
 What we need 
 Symbotic is seeking a Senior Manager, Strategic Sourcing to join our Strategic Sourcing team within our Supply Chain organization. Your role will be to lead our contract manufacturing strategy and develop a resilient, cost-competitive global manufacturing network for complex electromechanical products.

 What we do 
 Our global procurement organization partners closely with the business to build category strategies that drive competitive advantage. We own strategic sourcing and supplier agreements end-to-end — from commercial and pricing structures through supplier relationship management — while our sourcing operations ensure disciplined execution at scale. Our scope spans the full lifecycle: procuring robotics, structural, and automation components at the core of our systems, sourcing third-party partners for installation and deployment, and ensuring robust aftersales support once systems are live — all in service of Symbotic's commitment to reimagining the supply chain and transforming the movement of goods through intelligent automation, while bringing unparalleled value to the customer. Every decision is grounded in a relentless focus on total cost of ownership, balancing speed and rigor to drive the best outcomes for the business.

 What you'll do 
 Lead Symbotic's contract manufacturing strategy, including selection, negotiation, onboarding, and ongoing management of global manufacturing partners.
 Own commercial relationships with key contract manufacturers and assembly suppliers, driving cost, quality, delivery, and capacity performance.
 Develop and execute sourcing strategies for complex electromechanical products, partnering closely with Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Quality, and Manufacturing teams.
 Negotiate long-term supply agreements, manufacturing service agreements (MSAs), pricing, tooling, inventory, and capacity commitments.
 Drive annual cost reduction initiatives through value engineering, should-cost analysis, productivity programs, and supply base optimization.
 Support new product introduction (NPI) and production ramp activities to ensure suppliers meet schedule, quality, and cost objectives.
 Lead executive-level supplier business reviews and establish performance management scorecards and corrective action processes.
 Assess and mitigate supply chain risks related to capacity, geographic concentration, financial stability, and component availability.
 Partner with commodity sourcing teams across mechanical, electronics, motors, batteries, and other key categories to optimize total system cost.
 Develop manufacturing footprint strategies to support business growth, scalability, resiliency, and customer requirements.
 Manage significant annual spend and contribute to long-range supply chain, inventory, and working capital strategies.
 Build and mentor a high-performing sourcing organization as the business scales. 
 
 What you'll need 
 Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management , Business Administration, Engineering, or a related field; Master’s degree or MBA is highly preferred.   
 Minimum 8–10 years of strategic sourcing, supply chain, manufacturing, or procurement experience in robotics, automation, industrial equipment, electronics, or other complex hardware industries.
 Minimum 3 years of people management experience leading and growing teams.
 Deep experience managing contract manufacturers or similar EMS/mechanical assembly providers.
 Proven track record negotiating complex commercial agreements and delivering measurable cost reductions.
 Experience supporting product launches, manufacturing transfers, and global production ramp-ups.
 Strong understanding of electromechanical systems, including mechanical assemblies, motors, electronics, batteries, and custom manufactured components.
 Ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders and effectively communicate with executive leadership and strategic suppliers.
 Demonstrated leadership experience managing teams and driving results in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. 
 
 Our Environment 
 Up to 20% of travel may be required. Employees must have a valid driver's license and the ability to drive and/or fly to client locations and company HQ.
 Employees may be required to use a personal credit card for business travel expenses, which are reimbursed based on the program guidelines. Eligible employees may receive a corporate credit card based on role and travel requirements, but a personal credit card may be needed during onboarding until the corporate card is issued.

R10104634 Plant Manager (Open)

Location:

Chester, VA - ASU

**How will you CONTRIBUTE and GROW?**
-------------------------------------

The primary function of this job is to operate large Airgas facilities safely and reliably by complying with regulatory requirements, developing and leading personnel, managing costs effectively, and developing personal skills and competencies. “Large” facilities generally are complex facilities that generally include multiple plants or technologies, supply criticality, 8 or more direct reports or multiple locations.

**Airgas is hiring for a Plant Manager in Chester, VA!**

 

***We are looking for you!***

 

* Work Schedule - Monday - Friday
* Comprehensive Family Benefits: Airgas offers a full benefits package designed to support your whole life, including Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, AD&D, and Disability Insurance.
* Support for Parents: We offer a 14-week paid child birth benefit to support growing families.
* Future Security: 401(k) Retirement Plan with company match, Tuition Assistance, Paid Holidays, Vacation, and Sick time.
Early Access: Your benefits start after just 30 days of employment 

 

**Recruiter:** Jacob ( Jacob.braithwaite@airliquide.com ) Phone: 980-445-9764 Call or Text 
 
 
 
**The primary function of this job is to operate large Airgas facilities safely and reliably by complying with regulatory requirements, developing and leading personnel, managing costs effectively, and developing personal skills and competencies. “Large” facilities generally are complex facilities that generally include multiple plants or technologies, supply criticality, 8 or more direct reports or multiple location** s. 
 
 
 
**Operational Duties:**

* This role encompasses a wide range of responsibilities, including fully supporting, accurately completing, and maintaining all company Health, Safety, and Environmental policies, procedures, and documentation as required.
* The Plant Manager III is ultimately accountable and responsible for site safety including employees, contractors, visitors and neighbors. Other essential tasks include meeting or exceeding company safety standards, demonstrating strong safety leadership and commitment and implementing and maintaining the training matrix and Airgas University training for the site.
* The individual in this role will own Key Operating Documents, maintain updated red-lines at all times, and display a detailed understanding of content and significance of each document. In addition to this, the job requires making plant and process decisions, performing process troubleshooting, establishing clear delegation of this authority to trained subordinates, fostering positive customer and intercompany department relationships, delivering the quality and quantity of product required by the business and executing predictive and preventive maintenance to eliminate catastrophic failures and unplanned maintenance.
Furthermore, the role includes developing annual maintenance plans and turn-around planning as needed and sets and maintains high housekeeping standards to exemplify and improve the company image. 

 

**Regulatory Requirements:**

* The individual in this role is expected to operate the facility in compliance with all local and federal governmental regulations Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Department of Transportation (DOT), Current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP), etc) and company policies. This role also includes maintaining and complying with all necessary licenses and permits, providing all regulatory training and maintaining documentation, reporting and investigating all incidents and ensuring corrective actions are complete.
Other key duties include k eeping plant hazard analysis current and displaying thorough knowledge of possible hazards and associated safeguards as well as adhering to Management of Change procedure. This role also ensures that all performance evaluations, hiring, promotions and assignments are free of any form of discrimination; Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC). 

 

**Safety & Compliance Functions:**

This role includes a commitment to strict adherence to company policies, safety guidelines, and procedural standards, as well as a focus on modeling exemplary safety behavior, leading by personal example, working to achieve “Zero Accidents” by taking a leadership role in safety, implementing and ensuring compliance to the Qualification and Training program for Production Technicians. 

 

**Communication & Collaboration:**

This role is expected to conduct an annual performance review with each employee, implement individual development plans annually and provide training and coaching to improve performance, provide candid constructive input to management decisions and actively support those decisions as well as adhering to administrative and operational policies and procedures. 

 

**Financial Management:**

* This role requires the understanding, monitoring and optimizing of operating costs within an authorized budget and the ability to identify and implement opportunities to reduce costs within delegated authorization.
* Additionally, the position involves participation in the Capital Planning Process and the Yearly Expense Budgeting Process . In addition to this, the job requires the c ontrol of overtime within established limits and c ontinuously improving efficiency and availability indicators and utilizing national purchasing agreements and frame agreements.

**\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_**
----------------------------------------------------

**Are you a MATCH?**
--------------------

**To perform this position successfully, an individual must be able to perform each job duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skills, and/or abilities required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential duties.**

 

**Required Education:**

Mechanical or Chemical Engineering degree preferred. Equivalent combination of education and experience acceptable 

 

**Required Length & Type of Experience:**

* 8+ years process industry experience.
Mechanical or Chemical Engineering degree is an advantage. 

 

**Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:**

 

* Technical and working understanding of the Air Separation or Carbon Dioxide liquefaction plant process or applicable process plant industry experience.
* Familiarity with regulatory requirements for operating plants, including Process Safety Management, OSHA regulations, EPA regulations, EEOC guidelines, FDA regulations (where applicable), state and local requirements.
* Strong computer and business application skills.
* Trainable on Distributed Process Control (DCS) or Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) operation and troubleshooting.
* Able to deliver and explain training material to operating personnel.
* Extremely organized and effective at time management – able to establish and maintain a plant filing system and control of engineering documents. Ability to read and red-line key operating documents.
* Displays mechanical and electrical aptitude for equipment operation and troubleshooting.
* Working knowledge of commercial agreements and Air Liquide customer relations.
* Excellent communication and team leadership skills.
High understanding of accounting principles and working knowledge of plant operating budget. 

 

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS:**

**The characteristics listed below are representative of the physical demands required by an individual to successfully perform the essential duties of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential duties.**

 

* Ability to work extended hours as business needs dictate.
* On call nights, weekends and holidays as required.
* Occasional travel required – typically 1 to 6 trips per year.
Willing to relocate for a promotional opportunity. 

 

**WORK ENVIRONMENT:**

**The characteristics listed below are representative of the work environment typically encountered by an individual while performing the essential duties of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential duties.**

 

* Frequent regional travel.
* Moderate overnight travel.
* Must have reliable, appropriate transportation.
Job requires visitation to various Airgas and customer sites, which have varying environments/conditions, layouts, and accessibility.

**Benefits**

We care about and support our Airgas Families. This is evident not only through our competitive compensation but also through a comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision plans, short-term and long-term disability, life and accidental death and dismemberment (AD&D) insurance, Employee Assistance Program (EAP), pre-tax commuter transportation benefit, parental leave, vacation, sick time, floating holidays, jury duty and funeral/bereavement leave, and paid holidays for all eligible full-time employees.

Additionally, we offer our eligible employees a 401k plan with company matching funds, tuition reimbursement, discounted college tuition for eligible employees’ dependents, and an Airgas Scholarship Program for dependent children.

Associates who are members of collective bargaining units should review their bargaining agreement to determine whether they are eligible for some or all of the benefits described here and to see any special terms or conditions for eligibility.

Airgas, an Air Liquide company, is a leading U.S. supplier of industrial, medical and specialty gases, as well as hardgoods and related products; one of the largest U.S. suppliers of safety products; and a leading U.S. supplier of ammonia products and process chemicals. record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
ABOUT GENESIS

We are a full-stack general-purpose robot company, born across San Francisco and Paris and bound by a single mission: to make general-purpose robots a reality, unlocking infinite physical labor for the world and freeing people for creativity, exploration, and the pursuits they love for their own sake.

We are French and American by birth and global by nature. We are backed by partners who share our vision, including Eclipse, Khosla Ventures, Bpifrance, and HSG, alongside Eric Schmidt, Xavier Niel, Daniela Rus, and Vladlen Koltun. Our people work across the Bay Area and Europe, building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model, and we are starting to put it to work with real customers.




THE ROLE

You own the supply chain for a general-purpose robot going from prototype to production: every part in the bill of materials, from actuators, gears and motors to structures, PCBAs, harnesses, batteries and sensors, and every supplier and manufacturing partner behind them. You build it from the ground up, in the United States and abroad, and you build the team that runs it. The scale goes from tens of units to hundreds to thousands, and the supply base, partners and processes that got us to today will not be the ones that get us there. Building the next version is the job.

This is a role for someone who has done it before, in the trenches, and wants to do it again with a product that matters more than the last one. You will spend your weeks with suppliers, on the floor with our manufacturing partners, in design reviews with the engineers who are still changing the parts, and with the leadership team on the decisions that shape the company. Strategy and execution are the same job here.




WHY THIS ROLE

Few people get to decide how a new category of machine gets built. Eno is dexterous, wheeled and already working with real customers, built today with a supply base and partners that got us here. The next version of that supply chain, the one that takes us to volume, is yours to shape: what we make and what we buy, where in the world it comes from, which partners we grow with, and what the robot costs at scale. Those choices will be visible in every unit we ship for years.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Strategy. Set the supply chain strategy from pilot to volume: make versus buy, regional footprint, domestic content for regulated markets, single versus dual source by sub-system, and the order in which each piece moves as volume grows.

Partners. Own contract manufacturer and partner relationships at the executive level: selection, agreements, capacity commitments, cost and quality performance, and the transfer of sub-assemblies between regions and partners when the plan calls for it.

Cost. Own the cost roadmap: should-cost and total-cost models, the path from pilot cost to target cost, tooling and capital decisions, long-term agreements with pricing that steps down with volume; partner with Finance on working capital and with Legal on supplier agreements.

Supply base. Build the supplier base for the hard sub-systems: actuators, gears and motors, machined and cast structures, PCBAs, harnesses, shells, batteries and sensors; two qualified sources for every critical part, in the regions the product and our customers require.

Risk. Run capacity and risk: capacity ahead of demand, lead-time and allocation strategy for constrained parts, tariff and trade exposure, geopolitical and single-point-of-failure risk, and a plan for each.

Team. Build and lead the organization: sourcing, supplier development, planning, supplier quality and logistics. Hire the leaders under you, hold a high bar, set the operating cadence and the weekly numbers (clear-to-build, on-time delivery, purchase price variance, inventory, supplier quality) and the readout to the leadership team and the board.

Systems. Stand up what a scaled organization runs on, with Manufacturing Engineering and Platform: part numbering, BOM and change control, MRP and ERP, supplier portal, traceability. Lightweight first, then more.

Design. Be in the design conversation from the start: bring supplier capability and cost into the product early, and push the design toward what can be built at volume at the right price.




WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

Built it before. You have led the supply chain organization for a complex electromechanical product from first builds through production at scale, and either built the supply base from scratch or moved it to a new geography. Robotics, electric vehicles, aerospace, consumer electronics or medical devices.

Leader of leaders. You have built a supply chain organization, hired its managers, and run it on numbers; you can still do the work yourself when the team is three people.

Commercial weight. You have negotiated with contract manufacturers and tier-one suppliers at the executive level and closed long-term agreements that held up under pressure.

Global. You have sourced across regions, including Asia and North America, and moved production between them.

Cost record. You can walk through a BOM cost-down from pilot to volume part by part, and you know where the money hides.

Technical. You read drawings and GD&T, you understand actuators, gearboxes, motors and PCBAs well enough to challenge an engineer constructively, and you are fluent in BOMs, change control, should-cost and MRP.

Pace. You default to urgency, operate without a playbook, and are comfortable before the systems exist.

Experience. Typically 10 or more years in supply chain, sourcing or manufacturing operations for complex hardware, with time in a mature organization so you know what good looks like at scale, and time in a company that was building it. Engineering degree preferred.




WHAT ELSE YOU NEED TO KNOW

On-site in the Bay Area. Travel to suppliers and partner sites, including international, up to 40%.




HOW WE WORK

We are always looking for people who are driven to work on hard problems and want to shape what the world will look like in ten years. A few of the values that guide us:

Limitless ambition. We hold ourselves to the highest bar in everything we build.

Relentless urgency. Iterate faster, learn faster. Time is the denominator.

Type-2 Fun. Take the work seriously, not yourself. Embrace the grind and find joy in the struggle.

Radical transparency. Candid communication builds trust, and direct feedback drives growth.

Multiculturalism. We come from across the world. Be curious. Meet people on their terms.

Team over ego. Help others, share context, and win as a team.

A joyful journey. We take pride in the craft, enjoy the ride, and make space to laugh. Happiness is part of how we get there.

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
The Plant Manager is responsible for coordinating, directing, leading, guiding, and managing areas of the plant consistent with company policies and procedures as well as with federal, state and local law. Will be accountable for the management and safety of employees, high quality products being produced, budgeting and the profitability of the facility. The Plant Manager develops processes that will maximize stewardship, safety, quality, culture, customer relations, and productivity. This role has direct supervisory responsibility for all operations management and hourly team members with an expanded dotted line responsibility for a variety of support groups when department heads are not present (i.e., Sanitation, Shipping, Maintenance & Engineering). Will work closely with Human Resources and production teams in hire and train staff.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**: This list is not intended to be all-inclusive and other duties may be assigned.

* Initiate and maintain a safe workplace in accordance with regulatory and plant policies by maintaining effective safety and ergonomic programs and proactively correcting deficiencies to meet company goals of an injury free workplace.
* Responsible for communicating necessary feedback updates, up through STF leadership that pertain to the shift's activities.
* Be an active member, leading and facilitating our Safety Committee.
* Implement and attain goals to reduce injuries and cost per claim of injuries.
* Responsible for team members for the overall direction, coordination, and evaluation of all shift operations; ensure all operating procedures are followed and correct and/or update when needed.
* Ensure employee safety training, assist in the identification of and correction of safety hazards and ergonomic issues.
* Ensure all staff and employees know and understand CCP's, HACCP and SSOP documents/plans.
* Maintain product failures and foreign material issues are kept at a minimum; continue efforts for improvement.
* Responsible for overseeing all plant activity within all departments of the shift including supporting areas.
* Serve as a contact person for vendors and suppliers.
* Initiate and modify as necessary methods of ensuring production goals are met, including product quality per food safety requirements and specifications, efficiency, hours, cost and safety to remain efficient and competitive.
* Develop and manage a system that tracks labor, product and packaging costs that result in a reduction to the budget.
* Carries out managerial/supervisory responsibilities in accordance with the companies policies and applicable laws.
* Responsible for plant labor, raw material utilization, yields, supplies and waste reduction to ensure they are being managed in the most efficient manner.
* Responsibilities include interviewing, hiring, training employees, planning, directing and assigning work; appraising performance; rewarding and counseling employees when necessary to maintain a high standard of employee relations.
* Facilitate training and development sessions that develops the skills and education of company leaders.
* Develop and manage a strong productive working relationship with the UFCW, Local 2. Ensuring compliance with our collective bargaining agreement.

**QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS**: To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the work environment, knowledge, skill, and/or ability required or preferred. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

**EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE**: Bachelor's degree in a related field (agriculture, animal science or business) plus ten years of plant experience or the combination of education and experience that enables performance in all aspects of the position, including supervisory experience. Well-developed management skills utilizing sound management principles in leading a team of employees.

**COMMUNICATION SKILLS**: Must have excellent written and verbal communication skills. Ability to write reports and business correspondence. Ability to effectively manage time and meet all specified deadlines.

**LANGUAGE SKILLS**: Ability to read and interpret documents in the English language such as safety files, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals. Must be able to effectively communicate with USDA, production and management personnel.

**MATHEMATICAL SKILLS**: Ability to apply mathematical applications to practical situations.

**REASONING ABILITY**: Ability to solve practical problems. Ability to interpret a variety of instructions furnished in written, oral, diagram or schedule form.

**OTHER SKILLS AND ABILITIES**: Ability to use computers and all standard programs used by the industry and the ability to learn and effectively use any and all other computer programs that are or will be made available.

**BACKUP PERSONNEL**: In the absence of the Plant Manager, the Plant Superintendent will assume responsibilities for overseeing food safety and quality assurance programs.

**MISSION, VISION, & VALUES:** Must believe and lead STF's **MISSION** of producing quality pork products, igniting the passion and growth of our team members, helping our community thrive, and making our business prosperous. Remembering that together we will achieve more by working safely and cultivating an inclusive and empowering environment. Must believe and fully engage in STF's **VISION** of being a place where we all belong, working as one, to build our future. Must live STF's **VALUES** in all decisions, behaviors, and interactions, which include-

SAFETY- Be committed to the safety and welfare of all employees through prevention, education, and awareness, with the ultimate goal of eliminating workplace accidents.

QUALITY- Our customers and families depend on us to provide a safe, quality product, by maintaining the highest food safety standards and desired customer specifications. Must take pride in the products we produce and serve.

DIVERSITY- We embrace diversity of identity, experience, and thought, and actively strive for inclusive behaviors across our company and our work. By promoting these values, we aim to create a positive work experience that encourage a sense of belonging.

COMMUNITY- Be a positive representative of STF in our community while supporting the organizations who work for the betterment of Siouxland.

SUSTAINABILITY- Be a steward of the earth by managing our environmental footprint.

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS**: While performing the duties of this job, the employee will be required to move about the facility. The employee is frequently required to stand; walk; use hands to finger; handle; or feel/hold objects; reach with hands and arms; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl; speak; hear taste and smell. The employee must regularly lift and/or move up to 10 pounds, frequently lift and/or move up to 25 pounds, and occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus. Individual must be able to effectively work in a normal production environment where temperatures and noise levels may vary.

*Are you a passionate leader energized by driving continuous improvement?* ***Winnebago Motorhome is seeking a Plant Manager to join our team based in Forest City, IA.*** *The Plant Manager leads overall operations of a soft goods manufacturing facility (cut-and-sew, upholstery, foam, and textile assembly). This expert-level role owns safety, quality, delivery, cost, and people (SQDCP) performance, deploying lean manufacturing systems (5S, Standard Work, Visual Management, Kaizen) and ensuring compliance with relevant standards (RVIA, OSHA, NFPA 1192, ANSI methods as applicable). Responsibilities include strategic planning, capacity and labor management, production scheduling, quality systems oversight, supplier and materials coordination, cross-department alignment, and talent development to achieve world-class operational results.*

**Day to Day of the Role:**

* Own plant SQDCP performance; establish and drive KPIs and tiered daily management (Safety, OEE, FPY, on-time delivery, productivity, scrap, rework, etc).
* Lead daily Tier 1-3 process, Gemba walks, huddles, and visual management; drive corrective actions and sustainment.
* Implement and sustain lean systems: 5S, Standard Work, Kanban/pull systems, value stream mapping, line balancing, takt-time alignment, TPM. (Lean Six Sigma Blackbelt Preferred but not required)
* Ensure compliance with industry and regulatory requirements: Industry and lean best practices, RVIA, OSHA, EHS, NFPA 1192, and ANSI methods as applicable.
* Oversee master scheduling, capacity planning, labor planning, and materials flow to meet demand with optimal lead time and cost.
* Champion quality: PFMEA/Control Plans, incoming/in-process/final inspection, root cause analysis (8D, DMAIC), containment, and standardization.
* Optimize cutting, kitting, sewing, upholstery, and final assembly workflows; reduce WIP, increase throughput, and minimize waste.

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 


Shield AI is seeking a senior Solutions Architect – Manufacturing to serve as the functional and technical authority for Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP across Manufacturing, MRP/Supply Chain Planning, and the shop-floor-to-ERP technology stack. This role owns the design, configuration, and continuous improvement of Oracle Fusion Manufacturing and MRP capabilities, with deep, hands-on strength in MES, QMS, and PLM — ensuring plan, build, and quality processes operate as one coherent, well-architected system.
This is a hands-on, business-facing role. The Solutions Architect is expected to be the trusted advisor and go-to resource for Manufacturing and Quality business partners on any process change involving Oracle Fusion Manufacturing/Planning or the MES, QMS, and PLM bolt-on applications — translating business need into a scalable, well-architected solution, and then configuring and implementing that solution directly for medium-complexity projects. For large, complex initiatives, this person leads solution design and partners with Shield AI’s implementation partner to deliver, while remaining the accountable architect and voice of the business throughout.
Beyond core ERP, this role holds full ownership of Shield AI’s manufacturing-adjacent bolt-on application landscape — including MES, QMS, and PLM (Teamcenter) — and is responsible for how those systems integrate with Oracle Fusion ERP to form a coherent plan-to-build-to-quality operating model. This role partners closely with the other Solutions Architects for Supply Chain and Finance on shared MRP/planning signals, supplier quality matters tied to Procure-to-Pay and end-to-end integration with Finance/Accounting.

What you'll do: 
Solution Architecture & Business Partnership
Designs and delivers technical solutions, creates detailed solution designs, specific integration points, and selects appropriate tools and frameworks. Collaboration with developers and engineers to implement solutions, conducts technical reviews and resolves design challenges.
Documents architectures, provides technical guidance during development, and ensures solutions adhere to performance, security, and interoperability requirements. Prototypes new approaches and evaluates emerging technologies for project suitability.
Serve as the primary point of contact and trusted advisor for business partners across Manufacturing, Production Planning, Quality, and Engineering on process design and system capability questions.
Act as the lead advocate for Manufacturing and Quality stakeholders in all ERP, MES, QMS, and PLM-related discussions, ensuring their operational needs, constraints, and priorities are represented in solution design.
Become the go-to resource for any proposed Manufacturing or Quality process change, evaluating impact, feasibility, and fit within the Oracle Fusion ERP data model and integration landscape before implementation.
Translate business requirements into scalable solution designs that balance standard Oracle Fusion functionality against configuration, extension, or integration needs.
Maintain a working command of adjacent end-to-end flows (Order-to-Cash, Procure-to-Pay) to ensure Manufacturing, MRP, MES, and QMS designs do not create downstream conflicts or gaps.
Hands-On Configuration & Delivery
Directly configure Oracle Fusion Manufacturing, Supply Chain Planning/MRP, Work Definitions, Quality Inspections, and related modules for medium-sized projects, enhancements, and break/fix work.
Build, test, and deploy configuration changes, including setup of Fusion functional areas, security, workflows, approval rules, and data structures related to manufacturing and planning processes.
Author functional design documents, configuration workbooks, test scripts, and process/procedure documentation to support changes made in the environment.
For large or highly complex initiatives, define solution architecture and requirements, then partner closely with the implementation partner to execute — remaining accountable for solution quality, business fit, and knowledge transfer.
Participate in and help lead workshops, fit-gap sessions, and design reviews with Manufacturing and Quality stakeholders and implementation partner teams.
MRP, MES & QMS Ownership
Own MRP and Supply Chain Planning configuration — planning parameters, supply/demand netting, exception messages, and planner workbench — ensuring plans translate cleanly into executable work orders.
Own the functional roadmap, configuration governance, and business alignment for:
– MES (Manufacturing Execution System) — work order execution, shop-floor data collection, routing/operation tracking
– QMS (Quality Management System) — inspections, non-conformance, corrective/preventive action (CAPA), supplier quality
– PLM – Teamcenter — engineering BOM, item master, and change management integration with Oracle Fusion
Ensure MES, QMS, and PLM remain architecturally aligned with Oracle Fusion Manufacturing and MRP, avoiding duplicate data ownership, conflicting BOM/routing data, or process gaps across systems.
Define and maintain the target integration model between MES, QMS, PLM, and Oracle Fusion ERP, including engineering-to-manufacturing BOM transfer and quality event-to-ERP disposition flows.
Partner with the Solutions Architect – Supply Chain on supplier-quality data flowing from Procure-to-Pay into QMS-driven supplier corrective action processes.
Integrations
Design and help implement integrations between Oracle Fusion ERP and MES, QMS, and PLM (Teamcenter), including BOM/routing sync, work order status, and quality disposition data.
Define integration requirements, data mappings, and error-handling/reconciliation approaches in partnership with technical/integration teams.
Evaluate integration patterns (API, middleware, file-based) and recommend approaches appropriate to data volume, latency, and criticality, particularly for shop-floor/real-time data.
Support testing, cutover, and hypercare activities for integration-related changes.
Governance & Continuous Improvement
Maintain configuration standards, documentation, and change control discipline for the Manufacturing, MRP, MES, QMS, and PLM functional areas.
Identify opportunities for process simplification, automation, and improved data quality across planning, production, and quality cycles.
Stay current on Oracle Fusion quarterly releases relevant to Manufacturing and Planning, and assess/recommend adoption of new features.
Mentor junior functional/technical resources and contribute to a growing internal ERP center of excellence.
Required Qualifications:
12+ years of progressive experience in enterprise ERP systems, with significant depth in MRP/Supply Chain Planning, MES, and QMS functions.
Hands-on experience configuring Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP (Manufacturing and Planning pillars); comfortable working directly in the application, not solely at a requirements level.
Experience across multiple full-lifecycle ERP implementations (Oracle Fusion required; prior experience with Oracle EBS, SAP, or other major ERP platforms is a plus).
Direct, hands-on experience with at least one MES platform and one QMS platform, including their integration into an ERP environment.
Working knowledge of Order-to-Cash and Procure-to-Pay processes and how they interact with Manufacturing, MRP, and quality operations.
Demonstrated experience acting as a functional/solution architect — able to design solutions independently, not just execute configuration tasks handed down by others.
Experience partnering with or managing systems integrators/implementation partners on complex delivery efforts.
Strong business partnering and stakeholder management skills; comfortable being the primary escalation point for Manufacturing and Quality process questions.
Working understanding of integration concepts and experience partnering on ERP-to-MES/QMS/PLM system integrations.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience producing functional design documents, process documentation, and executive-level updates.
Preferred Qualifications:
Prior consulting background (Big 4, Oracle partner, or boutique Oracle Fusion implementation firm) strongly preferred.
Direct experience owning or integrating PLM (Teamcenter) with Oracle Fusion Manufacturing/Engineering data.
Experience in aerospace, defense, or other regulated/complex discrete manufacturing environments.
Familiarity with Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC) or similar middleware/integration platforms.
Oracle Fusion certifications in Manufacturing, Supply Chain Planning, or Quality.
Experience operating in environments with export control, ITAR/CUI, or other regulated data-handling requirements.
AI & Agentic Automation Capabilities:
Shield AI is investing in Agentic AI to accelerate and automate manufacturing and quality operations. This role is expected to actively identify, design, and help implement AI-driven automation across Manufacturing, MRP, MES, and QMS — not simply consume AI tools built by others.
Identify high-value candidates for Agentic AI automation within Manufacturing and Quality — e.g., planner workbench exception triage, shop-floor anomaly detection, quality non-conformance routing/CAPA drafting, and work order scheduling recommendations.
Design and configure AI agent workflows using Oracle’s embedded AI/ML and agentic capabilities (e.g., Oracle Fusion AI agents, OCI Generative AI, Redwood/AI-driven planning recommendations) as they become available across Fusion Manufacturing and Planning.
Partner with IT/data teams to define prompts, guardrails, data inputs, and approval/exception paths for AI agents acting on manufacturing and quality transactions, ensuring appropriate human-in-the-loop controls.
Evaluate and pilot third-party or custom Agentic AI tools (e.g., for predictive maintenance, quality defect pattern detection, MES data synthesis, or supply/demand sensing) and assess fit against the target architecture.
Use AI-assisted tools for day-to-day solution work — requirements analysis, test script generation, configuration documentation, and data mapping — to increase delivery speed and quality.
Bring or build fluency in prompt engineering and AI workflow design; prior hands-on experience with generative AI or agentic AI platforms (Oracle AI Agent Studio, OCI Generative AI, Microsoft Copilot Studio, UiPath/Automation Anywhere agentic features, or similar) is a strong plus.
Champion responsible AI adoption — data quality, auditability, and change management — when introducing agentic workflows into regulated, ITAR/CUI-sensitive environments.

Pay within range listed + Bonus + Benefits + Equity
 
Temporary employee offer package:
Pay within range listed above + temporary benefits package (applicable after 60 days of employment)
 
Salary compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, licenses and certifications, and specific work location. All offers are contingent on a cleared background and possible reference check. Military fellows and part-time employees are not eligible for benefits. Please speak to your talent acquisition representative for more information.

 At RTX, the world's largest aerospace and defense company, 185,000 great minds are united by purpose and inspired to make a difference solving the world’s most complex problems. With our three market leading businesses, world-class operations and investments in research and development, we offer capabilities and opportunity no one else can. Together, we push the boundaries of known science and find new ways to connect and protect our world.  

 Raytheon brings the strength of more than 100 years of experience and renowned engineering expertise to meet the needs of today’s mission and stay ahead of tomorrow’s threat. We deliver solutions that help our nation and allies defend freedoms and deter aggression, creating a safer, more secure world. Join us and help shape the future of aerospace and defense.

 Raytheon has an opening for a Sr. Production Control Lead supporting our Undersea Factory in our Portsmouth, RI facility. The successful candidate has experience with Material Requirements Planning (MRP) systems in a manufacturing environment and utilizes data-driven decision making to enable effective material and workforce forecasting. This role requires daily interaction with cross functional teams, programs, and business units to maintain and meet organizational goals and objectives. These groups include planning, production control, operations, quality, and manufacturing/test/design engineering.
  
  
 What You Will Do 
 Managing a highly visible area with 6 production control professionals reporting into this position.
 Set strategic vision, direction and plan to execute on short to medium term program and functional strategies and initiatives.
 Material Availability Analysis, Tracking, and Reporting.
 Manage Kit Readiness including working with cross-functional team in BOM, Material Master, Process Engineering, Operations, and Document Control.
 Releasing production schedules in multiple tools through the MRP system and confirming in shop floor system.
 Coordinates kitting process with multiple stores and consolidation areas.
 Provide production floor support including replacement part management, shop floor material staging, Work in Progress (WIP) movement through shared resource areas, completion of units in shop floor and MRP system, delivery to next step (inventory or shipment), and meeting MRP schedule.
 Control the physical disposition of nonconforming or specially handled material including Return to Vendor, purged material, WIP STOP per contractual restrictions, and configuration of components/sub-assemblies as required.
 Maintain integrity of the shop floor, MRP, and inventory systems through key performance metrics.
 Process piece part movement to support internal build requirements through subcontractors, internal shared resources, and other Raytheon Technologies facilities.
 This position is an onsite role in our Portsmouth, RI facility.
   
   
 Qualifications You Must Have 
 Typically requires A University Degree or equivalent experience and minimum 10 years prior relevant experience, or An Advanced Degree in a related field and minimum 7 years experience.
 Experience in Production Control, Supply Chain, Planning, Logistics, Scheduling, Operations, Manufacturing, or other production driven environments within manufacturing.  
 Experience with MRP/ERP systems.
 Experience leading daily team operations and/or comparable leadership experience.
  
  
 Qualifications We Prefer 
 Experience leading in a Department of Defense (DoD) environment.
 Experience in Special Program Access and other business systems, including shop floor data systems.
 Experience in Six Sigma, CORE, Lean Manufacturing processes, diagnostics, and continuous improvement.
 Experience driving financial performance, cost reduction, staffing, and budgeting.
 

 What We Offer  
 Our values drive our actions, behaviors, and performance with a vision for a safer, more connected world. At RTX we value: Safety, Trust, Respect, Accountability, Collaboration, and Innovation.
   
   
 Learn More & Apply Now! 
 Please consider the following role type definition as you apply for this role. Onsite: Employees who are working in Onsite roles will work primarily onsite. This includes all production and maintenance employees, as they are essential to the development of our products.
 
 Clearance Information: This position requires a security clearance. DCSA Consolidated Adjudication Services (DCSA CAS) , an agency of the Department of Defense, handles and adjudicates the security clearance process. More information about Security Clearances can be found on the US Department of State government website here: https://www.state.gov/m/ds/clearances/c10978.htm  
 
 
 As part of our commitment to maintaining a secure hiring process, candidates may be asked to attend select steps of the interview process in-person at one of our office locations, regardless of whether the role is designated as on-site, hybrid or remote. 
 
The salary range for this role is 132,400 USD - 251,600 USD. The salary range provided is a good faith estimate representative of all experience levels. RTX considers several factors when extending an offer, including but not limited to, the role, function and associated responsibilities, a candidate’s work experience, location, education/training, and key skills. 
 
 
Hired applicants may be eligible for benefits, including but not limited to, medical, dental, vision, life insurance, short-term disability, long-term disability, 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts, flexible work schedules, employee assistance program, Employee Scholar Program, parental leave, paid time off, and holidays. Specific benefits are dependent upon the specific business unit as well as whether or not the position is covered by a collective-bargaining agreement. 
 
Hired applicants may be eligible for annual short-term and/or long-term incentive compensation programs depending on the level of the position and whether or not it is covered by a collective-bargaining agreement. Payments under these annual programs are not guaranteed and are dependent upon a variety of factors including, but not limited to, individual performance, business unit performance, and/or the company’s performance. 
 
This role is a U.S.-based role. If the successful candidate resides in a U.S. territory, the appropriate pay structure and benefits will apply. 
 
RTX anticipates the application window closing approximately 40 days from the date the notice was posted. However, factors such as candidate flow and business necessity may require RTX to shorten or extend the application window.

**If you are currently employed at Smithfield, please log into Workday and submit your application through the Jobs Hub.**

Have a seat at our table. When you join Smithfield, you become part of something special – a company that's sustainably feeding people around the world, producing good food the right way with respect for our people, animals, communities and planet. With opportunities across locations and functions, a culture grounded in our Core Four values - gratitude, communication, respect and accountability - and a strong commitment to learning, collaboration, and innovation, Smithfield offers challenging and rewarding careers where you can grow, contribute and make a real impact. **Apply Now!**

**THE VALUE YOU’LL BRING:**

*The position summary states the general nature and purpose of the job. Overall accountabilities are defined in this section.*

 

As the **Director of IT Plant Systems** , you will lead the Plant IT Systems Managers and their teams responsible for delivering and supporting technology solutions across Smithfield’s manufacturing and warehousing operations. You will champion standardization, continuous improvement, and operational excellence by guiding your team to implement scalable, high-quality solutions that enhance productivity and support the company’s strategic initiatives. This role requires strong leadership, deep understanding of process manufacturing, and the ability to build trusted partnerships across Operations and IT, while establishing one consistent Plant IT operating model across the manufacturing network.

 
 

**WHAT YOU’LL DO:**

*The below statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by people assigned to this job. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required of personnel so classified. May perform other duties as assigned.*

* **Plant Operations Partnership:** Serve as the strategic IT partner to Manufacturing leadership. Ensure Plant IT Systems Managers build strong relationships with Plant Managers and leadership.
* **Plant IT Leadership:** Lead, coach, and develop Plant IT Systems Managers. Establish clear accountability for site coverage, escalation, performance, talent development, and service delivery.

* **Plant-Floor Engagement:** Build a strong IT presence in the plants through regular plant visits, operational reviews, and frontline engagement. Ensure IT teams understand production processes.

* **Operational Reliability:** Establish accountability for the availability and resilience of plant IT. Partner across IT to eliminate recurring issues, address root causes, and minimize disruption.

* **Technology Delivery & Site Readiness:** Provide Plant IT leadership for initiatives from planning and readiness through deployment, stabilization, adoption, and transition to support.

* **Portfolio & Priority Management:** Partner with Manufacturing and IT leaders to identify, prioritize, and govern plant technology demand. Balance safety, business continuity, and operational risk, regulatory requirements, business value, capacity, dependencies, and strategic alignment.

* **Standardization & Simplification:** Establish common Plant IT processes, standards, documentation, escalation practices, support models, and deployment.

* **Cross-Functional Coordination:** Act as an integration point among Plant Operations, Infrastructure, Cybersecurity, Manufacturing Technology, and Supply Chain.

* **Lifecycle, Governance & Risk:** Maintain visibility to plant technology assets, application dependencies, lifecycle risks, obsolescence, supportability, and cybersecurity exposure. Establish governance and escalation for risks that could affect production or business continuity.

* **Continuous Improvement & Innovation:** Identify opportunities to improve plant performance through better use of existing technology, process simplification, digital capabilities, and data.

* **Service Management:** Establish consistent expectations for incident, problem, change. Use service metrics, production-impact analysis, and recurring issue trends to improve Plant IT performance.

* **Executive Communication:** Provide concise, outcome-oriented visibility to Manufacturing and IT leadership regarding technology performance, major incidents, investment priorities, and value.

* **People & Culture:** Build a high-performing, collaborative Plant IT organization through clear expectations, coaching, career development, succession planning, accountability.
 

 

**WHAT WE’RE SEEKING:**

*To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals to perform the essential functions.*

* **Education & Experience:** Bachelor's Degree from an accredited four-year college or university and 10+ years of relevant experience, or equivalent combination of education and experience, required.
* **Leadership Experience:** 5+ years of experience in team management/development required.
* **Manufacturing Expertise:** Hands-on experience with manufacturing systems is required, including MES, SCADA, automation, quality control, labeling, or compliance systems.
* **Technical Knowledge:** Proven experience leading teams that support and troubleshoot industrial PCs, labelers, scales, and RF scanning equipment.
* **Problem-Solving & Analysis:** Strong critical thinking, decision-making, and analytical problem-solving skills; self-directed and proactive in identifying solutions.
* **Collaboration & Communication:** Excellent interpersonal and communication skills with a proven ability to work across all levels of the organization and cross-functional teams.
* **Work Environment & Travel:** Must be able to travel up to 30%, depending on project and plant support needs.
* **Organizational Skills:** Strong organizational abilities with a track record of managing complex initiatives effectively.
* **Work Style & Values:** Respectful, approachable, and team-oriented, with a focus on fostering a positive work environment and strong working relationships.
 

 
 

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS & WORK ENVIRONMENT:**

*The physical demands described here are representative of those an employee should possess to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee may encounter while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.*

* The majority of the time is spent in an office setting outside of the production plant. The plant environment will include wet or humid conditions (non-weather related), extreme cold and heat (non-weather related), working near moving mechanical parts, exposure to fumes or airborne particles, and chemicals.
* Noise level in the work environment is usually moderate but can be loud when in the production area.
* Frequently required to sit; stand; reach with hands and arms; use hands to handle or feel; and talk or hear.
* Specific vision abilities required include close vision and ability to adjust focus.
* Regularly lift and/or move up to 10 pounds; Occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds.



Relocation Package Available

Yes

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, age, gender identity, protected veterans status, status as a disabled individual or any other protected group status or non-job characteristic as directed by law.*
