Application close date:
Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed. 
 At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!    
 
 
This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities. 
 
 At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We're working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

 This role is part of Blue Origin's Launch Operations organization, where our focus is launching and recovering New Glenn safely, reliably, and at an ever-increasing cadence. Launch Operations owns everything required to turn a rocket into a flight-ready vehicle on the pad and to recover and refly it, from vehicle preparation and integration to pad operations and booster recovery.

 The 9x4 is the next step for New Glenn: a larger, more capable vehicle with a nine-engine booster, built, stacked, and launched vertically. The design decisions made about it now will determine, for the life of the program, how fast, how safely, and how reliably we can assemble, stack, and launch it. As Director of NG9x4 Vehicle Operations, you will be the single leader thinking about the 9x4 from the point of view of the people who will operate it, and the voice of Launch Operations in every decision meeting about the vehicle.
 Reporting to the Vice President of Launch Operations, you will start with a team of about a dozen engineers. Together you will evaluate the vehicle design and the concept of operations and shape both, help define and install the tooling and facilities in our new vertical integration facility, and write the first draft of the work orders for final assembly of the booster and for everything it takes to get the rocket to launch. Some of your scope will also reach the new launch pad being built for this vehicle. If you are successful, you will go on to build the organization that staffs the vertical integration facility and builds and stacks the first 9x4.

 This is a mission-critical leadership role for Blue Origin. We need a leader who drives relentlessly toward results, unencumbered by the old way of doing things, and constantly inventing new ways to solve problems and perform our mission. This leader must not be afraid to get hands-on with engineers and technicians, on the tooling, in the facility, and eventually on the vehicle itself, when the mission requires it, including in the middle of the night. At the same time, your long-term measure of success is building in, from the start, a vehicle and a set of processes that let the Launch Operations teams assemble, stack, and launch at a fast, repeatable, "boring" cadence. You'll make the impossible look routine through detailed, quantitative, hands-on command of the work your team executes down to the individual work order.
 


 WHAT YOU'LL DO
 Be the Voice of Operations on the 9x4 
 Represent Launch Operations in all design, configuration, and readiness decisions for the vehicle, bringing the perspective of the people who will assemble, stack, and launch it
 Evaluate the vehicle design and challenge requirements, driving design changes that make final assembly of the booster, stacking, and launch easier, faster, and safer
 Bring the lessons learned from today's horizontal integration operations into the design of vertical operations, and question which of them still apply
 Partner with vehicle design and engineering, facility, and pad teams so that operations needs are in the design before changes become expensive
 Stand Up Vertical Operations 
 Help shape the tooling, ground support equipment, and other installations in the new vertical integration facility, and help get them procured and installed
 Formalize the concept of operations in greater detail: how the nine-engine booster is finally assembled, how the second stage and payload are stacked vertically, and how the vehicle is prepared and launched
 Write the first draft of the work orders for final assembly of the booster and for all of the preparation needed to get the rocket to launch, and set the standard for high-quality, executable work orders (clear, sequenced, measurable, and completable by shift) so launch readiness is derived from objective data
 Take on operations scope for work at the new launch pad being built for this vehicle
 Lead Execution and Manage Risk 
 Manage technical and schedule risk as the vehicle, the facility, and the tooling come together; when schedule slips, personally own and drive the recovery plan rather than simply reporting the slip
 Perpetuate a high-standard safety culture across all vehicle work, given the significant personnel, process, and material hazards involved
 Be willing to get on the ground with engineers and technicians to solve problems directly, at any hour, when the mission requires it
 Drive Cross-Functional Integration 
 Serve as the primary point of contact between the operations teams and New Glenn vehicle design/engineering, facility, tooling, and pad leadership
 Partner with the business operations function (scheduling and operations analytics) to maintain an objective, data-driven view of remaining work and schedule risk
 Build the organization's own engineering ownership and judgment over time, reducing reliance on borrowed engineering support from other Blue Origin programs
 Build and Lead a High-Performing Organization 
 Lead an initial team of about a dozen engineers, and grow it into the organization that staffs the vertical integration facility and builds and stacks the first 9x4
 Build, mentor, and develop a bench of leaders and engineers in a fast-growing organization
 Take difficult, immature processes and mature them into fast, repeatable operations that don't require nightly heroics to execute
 Foster a culture where every technician and engineer is genuinely excited about Blue Origin's mission and understands the "why" behind the work
 Champion the use of AI to reduce engineering workload (including work-order authoring) and to accelerate the ramp of less experienced engineers
 Deliver Results 
 Use your own data and numerical analysis to understand team performance, drive decisions, and communicate progress
 Set quantitative targets for the labor hours and calendar time to assemble, stack, and launch the 9x4, and shape the vehicle and the processes to meet them, so the vehicle supports a much higher launch cadence
 Present vehicle design, readiness, and risk to Blue Origin's most senior executive leadership, including with little to no coaching
 
 WHAT YOU BRING

 Minimum Qualifications 
 Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Aerospace, or Industrial Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience building and leading complex vehicle or aircraft programs
 7+ years of progressive leadership experience building, integrating, or maintaining complex vehicles, aircraft, or other high-reliability systems: aerospace, defense, marine, oil & gas, or similar heavy/complex-machine environments
 Experience representing operations, manufacturing, or production in design decisions, with a demonstrated track record of challenging engineering requirements and driving design changes to improve manufacturability or maintainability
 Leadership experience with budget and resource management responsibility for technical/operational organizations
 Experience leading multidisciplinary technical teams, with the ability to grow a team and lead through subordinate managers
 A specific, demonstrated track record of driving measurable rate or throughput improvements in a complex manufacturing, assembly, or operations environment
 A demonstrated track record of building and perpetuating a high-standard safety culture in environments with significant personnel, process, or material hazards
 Demonstrated ability to make high-stakes technical and operational decisions under schedule pressure
 Strong executive presence with excellent written and verbal communication skills; demonstrated ability to influence stakeholders at all levels, including senior executive leadership
 Strategic thinker with a bias for action and a track record of hands-on operational execution
 
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Direct experience in final assembly, integration, or maintenance of military or civilian aircraft, weapons systems, or launch vehicles
 Experience with vertical assembly or stacking of large vehicles or structures, such as launch vehicles, or comparable heavy lifting and integration
 Experience standing up a new factory, production line, or facility, including shaping the tooling and the concept of operations
 Experience writing the first work instructions or work orders for a new vehicle or product
 A track record of taking a new vehicle, aircraft, or complex product from first-unit production to rate production
 Hands-on experience as an aircraft mechanic (or similar trade) and/or as a manufacturing engineer
 Working knowledge of aerospace standards and workmanship requirements
 Experience building or scaling an engineering/technical organization from a nascent, dependent state to self-sufficiency
 Master's degree in a related engineering field, or an MBA
 Culture Statement 
 Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

 Export Control Regulations 
 Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

 Background Check 
 Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check
 Required for Certain Job Profiles:  Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation
 Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
 Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical
 
 Benefits 
 Benefits include:  Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program.
 Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)
 Paid Time Off:  Up to four (4) weeks per year based on weekly scheduled hours, and up to 14 company-paid holidays.
 Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company's intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company's results, or other factors at the company's sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details. 
 
 Equal Employment Opportunity 
 Blue Origin is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer and is committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly qualified and dedicated work force. Blue Origin hires and promotes people on the basis of their qualifications, performance, and abilities. We support the establishment and maintenance of a workplace that fosters trust, equality, and teamwork. We provide all qualified applicants for employment and employees with equal opportunities for hire, promotion, and other terms and conditions of employment, regardless of their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin/ethnicity, age, physical or mental disability, genetic factors, military/veteran status, or any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local law. Blue Origin will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the Washington Fair Chance Act, the California Fair Chance Act, the Los Angeles Fair Chance in Hiring Ordinance, and other applicable laws. For more information on “Know Your Rights,” please see here .

 Affirmative Action and Disability Accommodation 
 Applicants wishing to receive information on Blue Origin’s Affirmative Action Plans, or applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in the application and/or interview process, please contact us at  EEOCompliance@blueorigin.com . Please note this is a publicly managed inbox. Please do not include any personal medical information in your request.

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE TEAM

 Anduril Intelligence Systems (AIS) is focused on positioning Anduril as a lead provider of specialized engineering and products for Intelligence Community (IC) customers. We work within the IC to understand their requirements, shape their concepts of operation, and deliver exquisite capability across their problem set. We aim to develop and deploy critically needed capabilities that address our customers’ most pressing national security requirements.

 ABOUT THE JOB

 We are looking for a Head of Operations to join our rapidly growing Intelligence Systems team. In this role you will be responsible for all business operations for the business line you support. Your work will vary from quick-turn operational fire-fighting, to building and redesigning processes, to leading high-impact strategic projects. This role requires you to be a trusted partner to each part of the business, and to work with and support the Division leadership teams to achieve our strategic objectives.

 WHAT YOU'LL DO

 
 Partner to the GM — Serve as the right hand to the General Manager of Intelligence Systems, responsible for all internal operations of the business line.

 Act as COO of the business line — Drive day-to-day business operations for Intelligence Systems. This includes business planning & organization design, financial tracking, talent planning & people operations, staffing and hiring, corporate governance, go-to-market, real estate & facility planning, security & infrastructure compliance, proposal & legal support, and sharing the division's narrative — working with cross-functional partners across each of these domains.

 Lead the BizOps team — Lead the Business Operations team within Intelligence Systems, composed of a Business Execution/Services team and Business Analytics, with the potential to include Production Operations/Analytics.

 Own the bottom line — Own the business line P&L and burn rate. Partner with Finance and FP&A to track financial health against division goals, take action to keep operating expenses within budget, and recommend strategies to drive toward margin targets.

 Define growth strategy — Define the growth strategy for Intelligence Systems in partnership with the Intelligence Systems Leadership Team, and lead strategic initiatives in line with business line priorities.

 Enable the engineering mission — Support the growth, execution, and engineering of the business line with operational support.

 Scale the organization — Problem solve to enable the business line to operate as efficiently as possible and scale accordingly.

 Represent the business externally — Build senior leader engagement and external interface strategy (e.g., conferences, press releases, partnerships).

 Build partnerships — Build, negotiate, and execute partnerships across industry.

 Support M&A activity — Identify targets and engage in diligence.

 
 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 
 10-15+ years of professional experience in operations.

 Strong communication skills; trusted by executives and colleagues alike — Demonstrated ability to translate and articulate thoughts clearly and simply across a wide range of roles (software engineers, finance partners, recruiters, cross-functional leadership, and executives). Communications excellence across a wide dynamic range, both written and verbal. Experience interfacing with company leadership and executives is a must, with a demonstrated ability to cultivate trust, facilitate meetings for, and engage with executives.

 Technically minded — Solid technical aptitude and proven ability to understand technical designs, and the ability to work closely and effectively with engineering teams.

 Bridges operational and analytical teams — Strong emotional intelligence and ability to solve operational problems in a way that is both data-driven and people-centric.

 High ownership and capacity — Horsepower to effectively manage multiple (6+) large projects and priorities in parallel, at a rapid pace, and report out on progress regularly.

 Finance literate — Comfortable owning a bottom line, reading and acting on P&L, budget, and margin data in partnership with FP&A.

 Ability to work onsite five days a week at either our Reston, VA office or our HQ in Costa Mesa, CA.

 Minimum 25% travel expected.

 Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Top Secret security clearance.

 
 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 
 MBA or similar degree.

 Experience working with engineers and bringing hardware/software products to market strongly preferred.

 Experience in the intelligence community or national security mission space

 Experience leading a business operations, business analytics, or similar function

 Experience working effectively in a matrix organization structure.

 Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, Finance, or a related field.

 US Salary Range
 $183,000 — $243,000 USD 


 The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including: 

 

 Benefits 

 At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits . 

 

 
 Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams 

 Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.



 
 To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

 
 
 No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.



 Please always verify communications: 
 
 Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.

 Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com . 

 


 
 Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.



 
 What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com . Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.



 


 

 Data Privacy 

 To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/ . 

 

 By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

RELOCATION ASSISTANCE: Relocation assistance may be available 
 
CLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: No 
 
CLEARANCE TYPE: Secret 
 
TRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the Time Description 
 
At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history. 
 
 
 The Director, Manufacturing Engineering provides functional and strategic leadership for the manufacturing engineering organization, accountable for process capability, producibility, and product quality across production programs. This role leads a team of managers and engineers responsible for developing, deploying, and continuously improving manufacturing, test, and related industrial engineering processes to meet safety, quality, delivery, cost, and people objectives in Baltimore, MD .

 Key Responsibilities
 Functional & People Leadership Lead and develop a high‑performing manufacturing engineering organization, including managers, engineers, and supporting staff.
 Define and maintain functional standards, methods, tools, and best practices for manufacturing engineering across the site or business.
 Recruit, develop, and retain talent; drive succession planning, leadership development, and engagement/inclusion activities.
 Provide regular coaching, performance feedback, and career development for managers and engineers.
 
 
 Manufacturing Engineering Ownership Own manufacturing engineering processes from new product introduction through sustainment, ensuring robust process controls, standard work, and documented work instructions.
 Direct the creation and maintenance of MBOMs, routings, work instructions, tooling, and strategies that enable safe, efficient, and high‑quality production.
 Drive producibility into designs by partnering with Design Engineering early in the lifecycle; ensure effective transition to production and rate readiness.
 Establish and manage key performance indicators (yields, scrap, rework, cycle time, labor efficiency) and drive continuous improvement using data‑driven methods.
 
 
 Operations, Quality, and Continuous Improvement Partner closely with Operations, Quality & Mission Excellence, and Supply Chain to ensure stable processes and timely resolution of production issues.
 Oversee manufacturing engineering participation in MRB and nonconformance disposition; ensure effective root‑cause analysis and corrective/preventive actions.
 Champion initiatives to improve safety, quality, delivery, and cost.
 Lead manufacturing engineering support to factory readiness, capacity planning, and rate ramp‑ups.
 
 
 Program, Financial, and Strategic Management Align functional objectives, resources, and priorities with program and business needs; balance near‑term execution with long‑term capability development.
 Partner with Program Management and Business Management to support bids, proposals, and program execution, including manufacturing scope, risk, and cost/schedule inputs.
 Own manufacturing engineering budgets (labor, capital, and expense) and apply sound financial management.
 Develop and execute technology roadmaps and capital investment plans for manufacturing processes, equipment, and facilities.
 
 
 Compliance, Governance, and Stakeholder Management Ensure manufacturing engineering processes comply with regulatory requirements, customer standards, and internal procedures.
 Represent manufacturing engineering in internal and external reviews, audits, and customer engagements.
 Build strong relationships with sector/site leadership, program teams, and functional peers to drive alignment and resolve cross‑functional constraints.
 
 
 Basic Qualifications 
 Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related discipline with 10 or more years of relevant experience; OR a Master’s degree in Engineering or a related discipline with 8 or more years of relevant experience.
 3 or more years of functional management experience leading organizations of at least 100 employees.
 Progressive leadership experience in manufacturing/production, operations, program management, testing, or a related area, including direct leadership of engineers and/or first‑line managers.
 Demonstrated experience in manufacturing or production engineering supporting complex hardware (e.g., aerospace, defense, electronics, or similar).
 Proven track record of improving manufacturing and test processes, yields, cycle times, and product quality using data and metrics.
 Working knowledge of manufacturing process controls, quality systems, and relevant industry/regulatory standards.
 Demonstrated financial acumen including budgets, rates, and cost management
 Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to clearly present technical and operational content to leadership and customers.
 U.S. citizenship and an ability to obtain U.S. Government Secret security clearance or greater; OR DoE equivalent or greater
 
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Advanced degree in Engineering, Engineering Management, Business Administration, or related field.
 Experience in a Director or senior manager role leading a manufacturing engineering or test engineering organization in an aerospace/defense or similarly regulated environment.
 Experience working across multiple disciplines (design, manufacturing, and test engineering) with a strong focus on product development, producibility, and transition to production.
 Hands‑on experience with continuous improvement frameworks
 Experience managing capital equipment roadmaps and facilities upgrades to support long‑term manufacturing capacity and capability.
 Proven ability to build and develop high‑performing teams, including succession planning, leadership development, and engagement initiatives.
 Experience supporting proposals and customer reviews, including articulation of manufacturing engineering approaches, risks, and mitigations.
 Experience working in a matrixed organization, balancing program demands with functional standards and development needs.
 
 
 
Primary Level Salary Range: $194,600.00 - $292,000.00 
 
The above salary range represents a general guideline; however, Northrop Grumman considers a number of factors when determining base salary offers such as the scope and responsibilities of the position and the candidate's experience, education, skills and current market conditions. 
 
Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay. Annual bonuses are designed to reward individual contributions as well as allow employees to share in company results. Employees in Vice President or Director positions may be eligible for Long Term Incentives. In addition, Northrop Grumman provides a variety of benefits including health insurance coverage, life and disability insurance, savings plan, Company paid holidays and paid time off (PTO) for vacation and/or personal business. 
 
The application period for the job is estimated to be 20 days from the job posting date. However, this timeline may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates. 
 
Northrop Grumman is an Equal Opportunity Employer, making decisions without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, national origin, age, veteran status, disability, or any other protected class. For our complete EEO and pay transparency statement, please visit http://www.northropgrumman.com/EEO. U.S. Citizenship is required for all positions with a government clearance and certain other restricted positions.

### **Director of Quality and Informatics**

**Status:** Full-time **| Location:** Remote (AZ) w/ Occasional On-Site Presence in Tempe 
**Department:** Quality Management | **Reports To:** CMO 
**FLSA Status:** Exempt | **Pay Class:** Salary 
**Salary Range:** $79,793.00 - $105,455.00

SCHEDULE: 40 HOURS WEEKLY, MONDAY-FRIDAY

### **Position Summary**

The Director of Quality and Informatics plays a pivotal leadership role in ensuring the delivery of high-quality, data-informed behavioral healthcare services. This position is responsible for overseeing quality improvement initiatives, clinical data analysis, and informatics strategies that drive performance outcomes, enhance client care, and support regulatory compliance. The Director will lead their team in developing, implementing, and monitoring evidence-based practices, performance metrics, and data systems. This individual will play a pivotal role in driving population health outcomes across all service lines and advancing the organization's value-based care initiatives.This role requires a dynamic individual with a strong background in healthcare quality, informatics, and behavioral health operations who can bridge clinical excellence with data-driven decision-making.

At CPR, we are committed to making diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging an integral part of our daily operations. We strive to hire and retain talented, diverse, and creative individuals, and we are dedicated to ensuring equitable treatment by promoting fairness and respect at every level of our organization.

### **Knowledge and Skills**

* Experience in clinical quality management, regulatory compliance, and outcome measurement
* Proven leadership and team development skills across interdisciplinary teams
* Knowledge of federal and state regulations, including Board of Medical Facilities Licensing (BMFL), Arizona Health Care Cost Containment System (AHCCCS), and Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS), as well as the standards for healthcare quality and compliance.
* Well developed understanding of best clinical practices and evidence -based treatment models for behavioral health
* Extensive knowledge of population health, value-based care models, and risk stratification
* Ability to analyze complex data to inform strategic decisions and drive improvement
* Strong project management and process improvement expertise
* Proficiency with healthcare IT systems (EHR, HIE, data integration)
* Excellent verbal and written communication for reporting and stakeholder engagement
* Understanding of Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) and their impact on health outcomes

### **Primary Duties and Responsibilities**

* Lead initiatives to enhance clinical quality, including process improvements, audits, and compliance with regulatory standards
* Manage technology systems to support quality improvement and clinical performance, including overseeing EHR optimization and data integration
* Oversee population health management programs, including monitoring and reporting on Value-Based Contracts (VBC) and shared savings agreements
* Collaborate with health plans and other stakeholders to develop and implement targeted interventions for improving patient outcomes and addressing SDOH
* Facilitate cross-functional meetings to ensure alignment with business goals, including regular reviews of VBC performance, quality metrics, and operational efficiencies
* Conduct data analysis and report on performance, outcomes, and opportunities for improvement across all departments
* Lead special projects to drive innovation and efficiency, including Targeted Investments (TI) and Data Analytics & Performance (DAP) initiatives
* Provide oversight of client satisfaction surveys and ensure continuous feedback loops to improve service delivery
* Develop and maintain key strategic partnerships to ensure the success of population health initiatives, with a focus on behavioral health integration
* Provide departmental leadership and supervision to direct reports, including performance management, coaching, hiring, and training
* Manage the department’s budget, resources, and operational strategies to support departmental goals.
* Reliable and predictable attendance is an essential job function.
* Other duties as assigned

### **Qualifications and Education Requirements**

* Bachelor’s degree in Social Work, Counseling, Healthcare Administration, or related field required.
* Minimum of 2 years in a management or supervisory role in behavioral health or healthcare required.
* Master’s degree in Social Work, Counseling, Healthcare Administration, or related field preferred but not required.
* Current, unrestricted license issued by the Arizona Board of Behavioral Health Examiners: LCSW (Licensed Clinical Social Worker), LPC (Licensed Professional Counselor), Ph.D (Doctor of Philosophy), Psy.D (Doctor of Psychology) preferred but not required.

### **Other Requirements**

* Provide evidence of professional liability insurance coverage in the amount acceptable, minimum $1/$3 million.
* Must comply with training and supervision requirements during first 90 days of employment, and throughout employment.
* All licensed, certified, and registered staff will be monitored regarding restrictions.
* Appropriate reference checks by letter and telephone as requested.
* State-required background check.
* Medicare/Medicaid sanctions, criminal violations, subsequent malpractice actions, and any settlement(s) made on behalf of practitioners.
* Within seven (7) days of hire, apply for and/or present and maintain a Class One Fingerprint Clearance card. If application is necessary, a copy must be submitted for inclusion in the personnel file until card (and/or renewals) is received.
* All required renewals must be submitted 30 days prior to expiration date. It is the duty of the licensee to keep all renewals active and current and report any mandated changes to Arizona Board of Behavioral Health Examiners immediately.

**Advancing medicine to save lives. Together.**

Thanks to many decades of experience and our passion for what we do, we make an essential contribution to the global availability of biopharmaceuticals, especially for patients with rare and serious diseases.

Rentschler Biopharma SE is a leading contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) focused exclusively on client projects. We offer customized full-service solutions for bioprocess development and the production of complex biopharmaceuticals. As a German family-owned company with an international footprint and global reach, we combine experts, expertise and years of experience to develop best-in-class solutions – together with our clients.

Rentschler Biopharma has approximately 1,400 employees and is headquartered in Laupheim, Germany, with a site in Milford, MA, USA. In 2024, we joined the United Nations Global Compact, underlining our commitment to sustainability.

As an independent family-owned company, we live by the motto: Many hands, many minds - ONE TEAM! Open, respectful cooperation characterizes our working environment, where quality awareness, diligence and responsibility are our top priorities. With all the diversity of our talents in the Rentschler team, we pursue one vision together: advancing medicine to save lives.

As a member of the QC leadership team in Milford, the Director, Quality Control Technical Services will manage and oversee a Quality Control team responsible for maintaining GxP systems and processes that support site business objectives; within QC this will be from Clinical Development to Clinical Supply and/or Commercial manufacture at a Contract Development & Manufacturing Organization (CDMO). The candidate will work in close collaboration with Manufacturing, Supply Operations, Process Sciences and Quality Assurance to support continual improvement and cGMP compliance. The Director will work functionally as well as part of a multi-disciplinary team to support the development and approval of our clinical development programs, commercial operations, and implement strategic imperatives within a fast-paced environment.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

 

* Will manage teams of professionals within Quality Control encompassing raw materials testing, microbiology, QC LIMS master data and electronic systems, analytical equipment lifecycle management, documentation and data integrity
* Hire and develop employees within the department through coaching and mentorship while setting clear expectations for success
* Leads and manages the Milford Site QC Leadership team meetings and follow up action plans
* Establish and maintain Quality Control systems and processes at Milford, MA site
* Develops and maintains department budgets (expense and capital) in alignment with overall organizational goals for profitability

* Acts as portfolio manager for QC project work including scheduling, prioritizing and resource planning to ensure client contract deliverables are met
* Represents QC at the project team level and interacts with Rentschler clients as needed
* Ensure timely execution of client projects and clear communications to clients
* Identify and initiate improvements to Quality Control Systems and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), ensuring compliance with all relevant quality standards and regulatory requirements
* Verify & establish department readiness for audits by both internal and external authorities, serve as primary Quality Control contact for regulatory inspections and client audits
* Analyze regulatory authorities’ programs, guidance documents and activities in areas relevant to testing biological products
* Consistently advise site and Quality management of potential and actual actions that could adversely affect the business; represent quality exposures or represent opportunities to be pursued
* Collect and report quality control metrics via Quality Management Reviews and the Quality Council
* Promotes a strong Quality Culture based on the Rentschler core values

**Qualifications and Key Characteristics**

 

* BS required, MS preferred in a scientific/technical discipline with 15+ years of experience in a QC position within the biological and/or CDMO industry
* 10+ years in a management/leadership role(s)
* PhD in a scientific/technical discipline a plus
* Experience in microbiological methods and contamination control
* Subject matter experiment in laboratory equipment qualification and data management
* Ability to apply GMP regulations and international guidelines to all aspects of the position
* Experience with regulatory inspections and client audits specifically within a startup/early phase and commercial QC laboratories
* Extensive experience with writing and managing investigations and risk assessments
* Proficient in MS Office application suite as well GMP electronic applications such as LIMS
* Outstanding leadership abilities with demonstrated analytical and critical thinking skills while managing high performing teams
* Proven leader, delegator, and decision maker with the ability to interact with all levels
* Executive presence with strong interpersonal and communication skills, verbal and written

**Working Conditions**

 

* Manufacturing environment with potential chemical, electrical and physical hazards
* Personal protective equipment must be worn in the laboratories according to Rentschler safety requirements
* Exposure to cool/hot storage conditions
* May be working in a loud area at times, that requires hearing protection and other protective equipment to be worn
* Working around chemicals such as solvents, acids, bases and reactive or flammable materials
* May require immunization before performing work within the manufacturing area
* Pace may be fast and job completion demands may be high
* Some international travel (no more than 5% time)

**Physical Requirements**

 

* May be required to stand for long periods of time while performing physical duties
* May be required to lift up to 10 lbs
* Must be able to work safely with materials and equipment
* PPE as required

Base Pay Range

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities.

**About Blue Origin** 
We are a team of collaborators, doers, and problem-solvers who are relentlessly committed to a culture of safety. These positions will directly impact the history of space exploration and will require your commitment and detailed attention towards safe and repeatable spaceflight. Join us in lowering the cost of access to space and enabling Blue Origin's vision of millions of people living and working in space to benefit Earth.

 

As a Sr. Director for Manufacturing at Blue Origin’s manufacturing, production, and launch facilities, this role will have a direct impact on the success of Blue’s mission.

We are looking for senior leaders to apply their technical expertise, leadership skills, and commitment to quality to positively impact safe human spaceflight. Passion for our mission and vision is required.

 

**About This Opportunity** 
Blue Origin is actively building its senior manufacturing and operations leadership team across multiple sites. We are seeking an experienced Sr. Director with a strong aerospace background to lead high-performing teams in support of our rocket production program. This role will span the following functional areas:

Manufacturing and Integration
 
Provides senior leadership across production operations including structural fabrication, thermal protection systems, systems integration, testing, and final assembly for Blue Origin’s booster manufacturing. Responsible for establishing and maintaining process controls, driving production efficiency, and ensuring safe, repeatable spaceflight hardware delivery at all stages of the product lifecycle. This role will also provide leadership across integration operations supporting the assembly and verification of complex space systems, launch vehicles, and propulsion hardware. Accountable for coordinating cross-functional teams to ensure the safe, on-time integration of hardware in alignment with engineering requirements, mission assurance standards, and program milestones.

**Key Responsibilities:** 
Leaders across these functional areas are expected to:
 

* Lead and develop teams of Managers, Senior Managers, and Directors driving manufacturing and operations execution across space and propulsion programs
* Champion a culture of safety, quality, and continuous improvement across all functional teams
* Own departmental KPIs, budgets, staffing plans, and capital project portfolios
* Partner with Program Management, Site Leadership, and cross-functional stakeholders to meet production schedules and customer expectations
* Drive process definition, development, deployment, and improvement initiatives including Lean Manufacturing and root cause analysis
* Collaborate with engineering teams to advance Design for Manufacturability principles and accelerate the transition from development to production
* Implement and mature production frameworks that support world-class manufacturing capabilities
* Communicate and enforce mission assurance and safety principles throughout the organization
* Recruit, develop, coach, and mentor talent at all levels of the organization

 
**Minimum Qualifications:** 

* Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Manufacturing, Industrial, Aerospace, or Electrical Engineering, or equivalent experience
* 15 or more years of progressive experience in aerospace manufacturing or a closely related industry, such as launch vehicles, aircraft, spacecraft systems, or defense
* 5 or more years in a senior leadership role managing managers and large, cross-functional teams
* Demonstrated experience leading manufacturing and operations teams in fast-paced, complex environments

 

**Preferred Qualifications:** 

* Master's degree, MBA, or advanced degree in a relevant engineering or business field
* Prior experience in aerospace environments supporting space hardware, rocket propulsion, or other mission-critical, high-value components

You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

 

**Export Control Regulations**

* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical

* Reviews and proposes projects involving functional or organizational changes within the operation; builds the business case and tracks realized benefit.

**Operations & Production Standards**

* Resolves priority conflicts across lines and ensures lines are balanced and performing according to planning system rules.

**Continuous Improvement & Growth**

* Drives volume growth and productivity improvement by implementing Lean and continuous improvement methodologies across coating, curing, digital print, and material handling operations.

**Safety, Quality & Compliance**

* 5+ years of experience in successful manufacturing operations, with demonstrated ownership of cost or P&L performance.

**Certifications & Licenses**

* Lean/Six Sigma certification preferred

Location: Philadelphia, PA, United States
 
Date Posted: Nov 10, 2026

**About Alvarez & Marsal**

Alvarez & Marsal (A&M) is a global consulting firm with over 10,000 entrepreneurial, action and results-oriented professionals in over 40 countries. We take a hands-on approach to solving our clients' problems and assisting them in reaching their potential. Our culture celebrates independent thinkers and doers who positively impact our clients and shape our industry. The collaborative environment and engaging work—guided by A&M's core values of Integrity, Quality, Objectivity, Fun, Personal Reward, and Inclusive Diversity—are why our people love working at A&M.

 
 

**The Team**

At A&M, the North American Data and AI team, IQx (Official name to be announced) SBU is combining A&M's market-leading execution with AI and digital expertise to help clients redesign processes, improve performance and achieve better outcomes. Come be part of the launch of this cutting-edge team that is making an impact on A&M’s future. Join us in making a difference.

 

We are seeking a Operations Director to join our team. This position is an internal role within A&M’s IQx operations team, reporting directly to the COO and Finance lead for IQx.

 
 

We value a healthy work-life balance and promote in-person collaboration by providing a flexible remote work arrangement with select days in the office, as needed. Ideal office locations are New York City or Philadelphia, but this is flexible.

 
 

We offer excellent opportunities for career advancement and building leadership skills. Our business is committed to each team member’s development, training, and exposure to business leaders.

 
 

**How you will contribute**

As an Operationsirector, your primary responsibility will be for program management, resource management, onboarding activities, supporting the growth for our business, and helping us thrive to achieve our goals. The Operations Director is expected to grow to support the operations functions of the IQx business more broadly. Your primary responsibilities as we launch will include:

* Lead program management for IQx, including planning, tracking, and driving to completion the initiatives that support the launch and growth of the business
* Support and drive internal initiatives, coordinating across stakeholders, managing timelines and deliverables, and reporting progress to leadership
* Establish and run IQx meeting cadences (e.g., leadership, staffing, and pipeline reviews), including agendas, materials, action tracking, and follow-up
* Help set up and scale the IQx practice, building the operating processes, tools, and governance that will support the team as it grows
* Go-to person for all staffing matters for our business unit
* Assess and plan future resource requirements, driving utilization based on a thorough understanding of current and future project pipeline.
* Build relationships across the business with internal stakeholders including Senior Management, Talent Acquisition, HR, Finance and Operations teams
* Effectively plan for, and advise on conflicts and issues, on a regular basis, prioritizing based on commercial needs and key skills available
* Build awareness of individuals’ performance goals and development needs, influencing resourcing decisions that further the continuation of business and individuals’ skill-set development
* Advanced use of staffing/ workforce planning tools, AI and reporting (for example Profinda, Claude, PowerBI) in measuring utilization and influencing staffing decisions
* Collaborate extensively with the wider Resource Management teams across North America and globally, as required by project needs
 

 

**Qualifications**

The ideal candidate will be excited about becoming a true strategic partner for our business. We are looking for people who are personable, knowledgeable, entrepreneurial, and fun. A unique blend of qualities that cannot be fast-tracked into existence. You possess desirable qualities such as being anticipatory, engaged, and respectful, which earns the respect of others. Other preferred experience includes:

* Program management experience, with a track record of leading cross-functional initiatives, managing multiple workstreams, and setting up operating rhythms and meeting cadences
* Resource Manager with several years of experience in a consulting firm or matrix organization; experience in Ops, HR or Recruitment role also beneficial for the role
* Able to effectively partner with Business Leaders and other Resource Managers in the firm, working closely with the wider North America Resource Management leads
* Excellent relationship building skills, communicating with Business Leaders and staff
* Able to manage staffing by efficiently prioritizing multiple competing demands and dealing with tight deadlines
* Able to present meaningful reporting insights to senior leadership, delivering key resourcing messages and driving agreed-upon actions
* Degree educated with several years of work experience in a professional services or corporate environment
* Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, and knowledgeable in AI as well as resource planning tools
* Previous experience using a Resource Management/ Planning tool would be advantageous but not essential
* Keen to take on responsibility and grow the role
* Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment, and drive positive change
* Strong time management skills with the ability to plan and priorities workload
* High degree of accuracy and attention to detail
* Use initiative to solve problems and make appropriate recommendations for resourcing decisions
* Works well under pressure and with challenging individuals
* Keen to take ownership of resourcing problems and motivated to deliver value
 

 

If you see yourself in this description, we want to hear from you!

 
 

*How will you grow and be supported?*

Our team prides itself on sustaining a culture that reflects our core values. We value integrity, quality, and objectivity in our work. We believe every day is a choice, and so we like what we do and with whom we do it. We embrace diversity, foster inclusiveness, and reward merit. We encourage and support our employees and communities through ongoing investments from leadership, social and networking events, peer-to-peer networks, Employee Resource Groups, volunteer opportunities, and pro-bono work. We are committed to promoting an inclusive environment in which all can develop, grow, and be supported.

 

**Your journey at A&M**

We recognize that our people are the driving force behind our success, which is why we prioritize an employee experience that fosters each person’s unique professional and personal development. Our robust performance development process promotes continuous learning, rewards your contributions, and fosters a culture of meritocracy. With top-notch training and on-the-job learning opportunities, you can acquire new skills and advance your career.

We prioritize your well-being, providing benefits and resources to support you on your personal journey. Our people consistently highlight the growth opportunities, our unique, entrepreneurial culture, and the fun we have together as their favorite aspects of working at A&M. The possibilities are endless for high-performing and passionate professionals.

 
 

Regular employees working 30 or more hours per week are also entitled to participate in Alvarez & Marsal Holdings’ fringe benefits consisting of healthcare plans, flexible spending and savings accounts, life, AD&D, and disability coverages at rates determined periodically as well as a 401(k) retirement savings plan. Provided the eligibility requirements are met, employees will also receive an annual discretionary contribution to their 401(k) retirement savings plan from Alvarez & Marsal. Additionally, employees are eligible for paid time off including vacation, personal days, seventy-two (72) hours of sick time (prorated for part time employees), ten federal holidays, one floating holiday, and parental leave. The amount of vacation and personal days available varies based on tenure and role type. Click here for more information regarding A&M’s benefits programs.

 
 

The salary range is $150,000 - $170,000 annually, dependent on several variables including but not limited to education, experience, skills, and geography. In addition, A&M offers a discretionary bonus program which is based on a number of factors, including individual and firm performance. Please ask your recruiter for details.

**Culture & Values**
--------------------

At Alvarez & Marsal, our core values of Integrity, Quality, Objectivity, Fun, Personal Reward, and Inclusive Diversity guide everything we do, shaping a culture rooted in entrepreneurship, impact, and integrity. We trust our people to take ownership early, contribute to meaningful challenges, and drive results that matter. We empower growth and champion diverse perspectives. Above all, we value doing the right thing. For those ready to roll up their sleeves, lead with integrity, and be difference makers, this is where it starts.

**Equal Opportunity Employer**
------------------------------

It is Alvarez & Marsal’s practice to provide and promote equal opportunity in employment, compensation, and other terms and conditions of employment without discrimination because of race, color, creed, religion, national origin, ancestry, citizenship status, sex or gender, gender identity or gender expression (including transgender status), sexual orientation, marital status, military service and veteran status, physical or mental disability, family medical history, genetic information or other protected medical condition, political affiliation, or any other characteristic protected by and in accordance with applicable laws. Employees and Applicants can find A&M policy statements and additional information by region here.

**Unsolicited Resumes from Third-Party Recruiters**
---------------------------------------------------

Please note that as per A&M policy, we do not accept unsolicited resumes from third-party recruiters unless such recruiters are engaged to provide candidates for a specified opening. Any employment agency, person or entity that submits an unsolicited resume does so with the understanding that A&M will have the right to hire that applicant at its discretion without any fee owed to the submitting employment agency, person or entity.

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
**Brand:**

Bagel Brands

**Bagel Brands is the parent company for your favorite breakfast brands, Einstein Bros. Bagels, Bruegger's Bagels, Noah's NY Bagels, and Manhattan Bagel. We believe in the bagel and how it has the unique ability to bring people together. Our team has a standard set of values and behaviors that allow us to spread a little more joy and happiness in the world. They let us laugh, smile, and enjoy each other’s company a little more. These are the behaviors that guide how we work, how we treat each other, and how we treat our guests. We believe that there is no better way to make someone’s day than with a warm, fresh-baked bagel and a heart-felt good morning.**

**POSITION MISSION**

The Director, Operations Excellence leads the strategy, team, and discipline that make it easier for our bakery teams to obsess over our guests and deliver great results every day. This role owns the enterprise operations engineering agenda for Bagel Brands — evaluating how work gets done, designing better ways of working, and building the team needed to test, scale, and sustain change across Field Operations and Support Center teams.

 

In alignment with Bagel Brands’ Mission, Vision, and Values, this role builds an organization that helps teams Take Ownership of better ways of working, Support Each Other through thoughtful change, and ultimately creates simpler, more consistent operations that allow bakery teams to Obsess Over Our Guests.

 
 

Department: Operations

Salary: $180,000 to $200,000

Annual Bonus: 20%

Long Term Incentive Plan: $30,000

 

**RESPONSIBILITIES INCLUDE, BUT ARE NOT LIMITED TO:**

**Strategic Leadership & Vision**

* Set the multi-year vision and roadmap for Operations Excellence, aligning priorities with enterprise strategy and Field Operations needs.

* Build and prioritize a portfolio of process engineering and continuous improvement initiatives across the bakery system.

* Represent Operations Excellence in senior leadership and strategic planning forums, translating field findings into enterprise decisions.

 
 

**Operations Excellence & Process Engineering**

* Oversee evaluation of bakery processes, workflows, and systems to simplify work, optimize labor investments, reduce waste, and strengthen performance.

* Guide application of Lean, Six Sigma, process mapping, and root-cause analysis across a portfolio of concurrent initiatives.

* Own the standard for future-state process design, balancing efficiency, guest experience, team member experience, and financial impact.

* Ensure the team produces process maps, standard work, and tools that translate solutions into repeatable bakery practices at scale.

 
 

**Testing, Piloting & Continuous Improvement**

* Set the standard for how the organization designs and governs operational pilots before broader rollout.

* Review pilot results with senior leadership and make scale, refine, or discontinue recommendations.

* Sponsor root-cause analysis on significant recurring challenges, ensuring solutions are sustainable rather than short-term fixes.

 
 

**Labor and Inventory Analytics and Systems Optimization**

* Own labor and inventory system optimization through consistent review of program enhancements, labor/inventory performance opportunities, and cross-functional partnerships with IT, Finance, and program owners.

* Create and maintain regular reporting for Ops teams that highlights opportunities for improvement

 
 

**Project & Change Management**

* Own the portfolio of cross-functional operational excellence initiatives from problem identification through sustainment.

* Set the organization’s approach to structured change management and ensure it is applied consistently.

* Maintain enterprise-level visibility to portfolio progress, risks, and business impact.

 
 

**Team & Field Leadership**

* Build, lead, and develop a team of Operations Excellence managers and professionals.

* Coach the team on problem solving, project management, and change leadership, building bench strength for future roles.

* Maintain regular presence in bakeries, partnering with Field Operations leaders to test and validate solutions.

* Identify successful practices within the bakery system and lead efforts to standardize and scale them.

 
 

**Cross-Functional Partnership & Measurement**

* Partner with Training, Technology, Marketing, Culinary/R&D, Supply Chain, Finance, and Development to evaluate the impact of enterprise initiatives.

* Represent the Operations perspective in cross-functional and executive-level project governance.

* Own the measurement framework used to demonstrate whether operational improvements are delivering results.

* Deliver clear, data-driven recommendations and portfolio updates to senior Operations leadership.

 

**LEADERSHIP COMPETENCIES (DIRECTOR / SENIOR DIRECTOR)**

* *Effective Communication:* Articulates vision and manages difficult conversations cross-functionally; communicates complex initiatives and navigates executive discussions.
* *Accountability & Ownership:* Owns budget and strategy and drives a culture of accountability; manages multi-team performance and champions data-driven decisions.
* *Adaptability & Perseverance:* Leads the department through major change and anticipates trends; drives change across functions and builds resilient teams.
* *Empowerment:* Creates space for innovation and mentors emerging leaders; designs structures for decentralized decision-making.
* *Curiosity:* Probes beyond surface issues and fosters a learning environment; benchmarks against top organizations and sponsors new ideas.
* *Self-Awareness:* Understands own leadership brand and exhibits humility; holds deep clarity on values and stays resilient under pressure.

 

**REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES**

**Required**

* 10+ years of experience in restaurant operations, operations excellence, continuous improvement, or a related discipline.

* 3+ years of experience directly leading and developing a team.

* Track record of leading enterprise-scale, cross-functional projects with measurable business impact.

* Strong strategic, analytical, and structured problem-solving skills.

* Strong portfolio and project management skills, with the ability to manage senior stakeholders and budgets.

* Demonstrated ability to influence and drive change at the senior leadership level without direct authority.

* Excellent executive presentation skills and ability to travel regularly to bakery locations.

 
 

**Preferred**

* Direct restaurant or multi-unit operations leadership experience.

* Advanced experience applying Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, DMAIC, or comparable methodologies.

* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt, PMP, Prosci Change Management, or comparable certification.

* Experience within QSR, fast casual, retail, or another high-volume, multi-unit consumer environment.

* Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree (MBA or related) preferred, or equivalent experience.

 

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS:**

This position requires regular travel to bakery locations across multiple regions, including standing, walking, and observing operations on-site, as well as the ability to sit, use a computer, and participate in meetings for extended periods. These requirements may be met with or without reasonable accommodation.

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
**Company Summary: PuraGraft, a Young Innovations Company**

PuraGraft represents the leading manufacturers of biomaterial solutions for bone and tissue regeneration. No single material can suit all medical requirements and indications. However, through PuraGraft® you have access to the widest choices of products.

At Young Innovations, we foster a dynamic environment where team members make an impact every day as part of a collaborative, inclusive culture. Together, we serve the dental profession and their patients, united in our mission of achieving a Lifetime of Oral Health™

We embrace diverse perspectives and encourage bold thinking, challenging traditional approaches with a bias for action. Whether you’re looking to expand your skills or grow your career, Young is here to support your goals and continuous learning. At Young, YOU are at the core of what we do.

**Position Overview:**

Reporting to the VP Quality Regulatory Affairs, the Sr. Manager, Quality Assurance will be tasked with ensuring Quality standards are met or exceeded in all facets of the multi-site operation. He/she will partner internally in the development and implementation of new or adjusted quality standards, policies, and procedures, as required at Kingwood, TX and Scottsdale, AZ.

**You’ll like this role if:**

* You enjoy leading a team, solving complex quality challenges, and turning data into practical improvements. You take ownership of compliance and thrive in a hands-on role supporting quality standards across multiple sites.

**Why You’ll Love Working Here:**

* Medium sized company – not too big, not too small – just enough to get things done and see your impact.
* Did we say benefits? Full medical, dental, vision, 401k, parental leave, paid holidays, paid time off, short & long term disability insurance, employee assistance program, and more!
* Lead and inspire a dedicated team, build meaningful relationships, and help your employees grow and succeed.

**Who you’ll work with:**

* You’ll report to the VP of Quality & Regulatory Affairs and lead Quality Associates supporting our Kingwood, TX and Scottsdale, AZ operations.
* You’ll partner closely with QRA, Sourcing, Distribution, and Production teams to strengthen quality systems and drive continuous improvement.

**What You’ll Do:**

* Act as the site’s Sr. Quality and Compliance Leader, and when necessary, as the site’s Designated Management Representative to ensure compliance with all regulatory, corporate and facility requirements.
* Ensure compliance of two sites.
* Ensure outstanding Quality System performance via monitoring and measuring of process performance, and driving any appropriate action, including issuing and follow-up on activities required for sourcing, warehousing, and distributing pharmaceuticals.
* Supervise & Manage Quality Associates and develop culture of collaboration and cross-functional success within the department and business.
* Reviews and monitors Quality metrics and reports trends, to determine if there is a need to escalate issues to the management.
* Perform, review and monitor the Quality Management processes which include but is not limited to:
 + Ensure compliance with FDA, DEA and BOP requirements, including DSCSA traceability of pharmaceuticals.
 + Oversee Regulatory activities associated with distribution licensing, drug distribution reports, and permits for warehousing and distribution of controlled substances.
 + inspection and product release, label approval, calibration, warehousing controls, record retention, document control, training, control of non-conforming product, quarantined Products, control of access and drugs storage, including temperature monitoring.
 + Host and manage internal and external audits. Ensure the site’s readiness for assessments and lead implementation of corrective actions.
 + Effectively assess processes and identify opportunities for improvement.
 + Review, Analyze and Report Statistical findings through critical thought and storytelling of key findings and opportunities to all levels within a matrixed organization.
 + Partner with other departments to identify critical to quality metrics, and support the operationalization of monitoring and management to deliver improved performance across processes.
 + Create effective and compelling visual materials/presentations that support the process/product improvement impact to the organization and adequately represent the impact to quality, cost and time.
 + Define, track, and monitor key success measures associated with Quality Management Systems. Successfully deploy and support change management and appropriate training plans.
* Manage document control functions, including creation, review, and approval of procedures, work instructions and all other documentation for the Quality System.
* Manage the complaint handling system, including trending and review to identify opportunities for improvement.
* Manage the training of the Site, by maintaining the training log, tracking training completion of training by site personnel, creating training content and hosting group training as needed.
* Develop and host the Quarterly Management Review
* Manage the Recall process, from notification, tracking responses & expenses, reporting, and closure.
* Develop, refine, and/or maintain quality standards, policies, and procedures for the facility, including identifying, recommending, and fully implementing changes, in partnership with corporate QRA and local operations teams. Other duties as assigned

**What You’ll Bring:**

* Bachelor’s degree in technical field.
* Minimum of 3 Years of experience managing manufacturing and/or distribution of pharmaceuticals.
* Minimum of 3 Years of experience having direct responsibility for managing a Quality group.
* Direct experience managing FDA or DEA Inspections.
* Demonstrated proficiency in verbal and written communication in English, with the ability to convey information clearly, accurately, and professionally across all levels of the organization.

**Travel Requirements**

* Up to 15%

**Work Environment:**

**Office Environment**

This position is based in an office environment and is primarily sedentary in nature. It requires regular use of standard office equipment, including computers, phones, photocopiers, scanners, filing cabinets, and fax machines. Some roles may involve wearing a headset and sustained computer use for 8 or more hours per day. Employees may be required to sit, stand, or walk for extended periods, and occasional bending, lifting, or carrying items up to 50 pounds may be necessary.

**Manufacturing/Distribution Environment**

This position operates in a manufacturing plant environment. The role routinely involves working around machinery, equipment, and moving mechanical parts. The facility may be subject to varying temperatures, loud noise levels, and airborne particles such as dust or chemical fumes, depending on the area of the plant. This role may require periods of standing, sitting, or walking throughout the workday. Occasional bending, lifting, or carrying items up to 50 pounds may be necessary.

Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus. While performing the duties of this Job, the employee is regularly required to sit; use hands to finger, handle, control, or feel; reach with hands and arms and talk. Hearing abilities required for this environment include being able to clearly hear and respond to audible alarms, production equipment, forklifts, and other machinery to maintain a safe work environment. Individuals must be able to distinguish and understand verbal communication including instructions, safety warnings, and team discussions, sometimes in an environment with moderate to high background noise.

*US: Young Innovations, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer and E-Verify participating employer.*
